title: Senior Cloud Engineer
description:
Imagine what you could do here. At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming phenomenal products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish. Apple Pay is transforming the industry in payments, transit and identity, and we're aggressively focusing on the customer's digital wallet experience. Our scale and security demands create unique opportunities for innovative and creative solutions which contribute to millions of customer's daily interactions.

The Wallet, Payments and Commerce (WPC) Cloud Engineering team is looking for an experienced Senior Cloud Engineer to take ownership of complex, ambiguous problems and drive cross-functional solutions that scale with our growth. In this role you'll independently lead significant pieces of our cloud platform, set technical direction on project teams, and raise the bar on quality, security, and customer focus across the organization.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 8+ years of Cloud infrastructure and platform engineering experience, with a track record of owning systems end-to-end in production.
  • Experience building platforms and platform-as-a-product… You think about internal developers as customers, and you've shipped paved roads that people actually want to use.
  • Kubernetes and Containers… Been there, done that, and now you're the person others come to when the cluster is on fire. You've owned multi-tenant, multi-cluster, multi-region footprints end-to-end.
  • Infrastructure as Code, with deep Crossplane and Terraform experience… You've designed composition and provider patterns at scale, not just consumed them. The console is for read-only.
  • Security-first architecture with Policy as Code (Kyverno, OPA/Gatekeeper)… You bake guardrails into the platform so the secure path is the easy path, and you can defend your trade-offs to security partners.
  • Public cloud expertise across AWS, GCP, and/or Azure… You know which services to use, when to use them, and — just as importantly — when not to.
  • GitOps and CI/CD with Flux, Jenkins, Kargo… Everything ships through pipelines, promotion is declarative, and rollback is a non-event.
  • Strong networking fundamentals (NATs, TCP/IP, DNS, load balancing, mTLS)… You can debug a cross-region connectivity issue without flinching.
  • Linux internals and systems-level troubleshooting… When the symptom is "it's slow sometimes," you know how to find the actual cause.
  • Microservices and distributed systems experience… You've designed for failure, not just success.
  • Experience with service meshes (Istio, Traefik, LinkerD) and observability stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, Sensu).
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor engineers, drive technical direction across a project team, and align solutions with business objectives in ambiguous, cross-functional environments.
  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or a related field or equivalent work experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 10+ years of work experience is highly desirable.

title: Software Asset Management Analyst #1853749
description:
About NDi:

Network Designs, Inc. (NDi) is a leading Federal contractor that specializes in designing, developing, and delivering information technology and network solutions for government customers. Founded in 1985, NDi's firmly defined core values have driven all aspects of the business, which have been paramount to our company's success and the establishment of an enjoyable workplace atmosphere. At NDi, we believe that our people are the cornerstone of our success, and we value collaboration, career growth, and winning ideas. Military Veterans Encouraged to Apply.

Job Description:

Network Designs, Inc. (NDi) is seeking a Software Asset Management Analyst to support enterprise software request fulfillment, software asset management, licensing compliance, and software governance activities within a Federal IT environment.

The Software Asset Management Analyst will receive and process software requests, validate requirements, coordinate fulfillment activities, support software standards and license evaluation processes, and maintain accurate software entitlement documentation. The position works closely with Government customers, vendor managers, Contracting Officer's Representatives (CORs), Product Owners, procurement personnel, and technical support teams to ensure software requests are processed accurately, efficiently, and in accordance with established governance and compliance requirements.

Requirements:

  • U.S. Citizenship is required
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance
  • This position is remote, candidate must reside in one of the following states: AL, AZ, DC, FL, GA, ID, MD, MS, NJ, NC, OK, OH, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WV

Qualifications and Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in a related discipline such as Business, Information Systems, Information Technology or a related field
  • Minimum of five (5) years of relevant experience in software asset support and/or IT service operations.
  • Experience executing structured intake, data entry, ticket workflows, and customer communications within an IT service environment.
  • Knowledge of software request fulfillment, vendor quoting, and procurement intake documentation.
  • Experience supporting enterprise software governance processes and standards-conformance workflows.
  • Familiarity with software asset management repositories and software installation protocols, including:
    • License keys
    • Installation instructions
    • Installation files
    • Product documentation
  • Strong analytical skills.
  • Ability to reconcile software entitlement and consumption data.
  • Ability to document assumptions, evidence, and analytical methodology to maintain traceability.
  • Ability to develop clear, defensible recommendations and written outputs.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to work within controlled repositories, workflows, and governance processes.
  • Ability to coordinate effectively across technical, acquisition, financial, and software asset management stakeholders.
  • Strong customer service and communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple software requests and competing priorities within a production service environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience supporting enterprise software asset management within a Federal or similarly complex enterprise environment.
  • Experience with software asset management, discovery, or service-management platforms, including:
    • Flexera
    • ServiceNow Software Asset Management
    • Belarc
    • Tanium
  • Familiarity with software licensing, entitlement reconciliation, and software compliance processes.
  • Experience working with Government software procurement or acquisition workflows.

Key Tools and Platforms

Relevant systems identified in the PWS include:

  • ServiceNow IT Service Management (ITSM)
  • ServiceNow Software Asset Management
  • iViews / IT Acquisition Request System (ITAR)
  • Flexera
  • Belarc
  • Tanium
  • FAA Enterprise Architecture Management System (EAMS)
  • Microsoft Power Platform
  • Microsoft Office applications

Responsibilities

Software Request Fulfillment:

  • Receive and process requests for enterprise software.
  • Ensure assigned requests are acknowledged and routinely updated in accordance with established service expectations.
  • Interface directly with customers to confirm that software requirements are complete, well-formed, and aligned with the intended purchase or fulfillment approach.
  • Track software requests throughout the fulfillment lifecycle and coordinate required follow-up activities through closure.
  • Coordinate with Vendor Managers, CORs, Product Owners, software specialists, procurement personnel, and other stakeholders as needed.
  • Request vendor quotes and coordinate funding requirements with customers.
  • Enter software purchase requests into the Government-designated IT Acquisition Request system.
  • Assign installation tasks and coordinate fulfillment activities with supporting technical teams.

Software Standards and Licensing Support:

  • Perform FAA IT Standards conformance checks for requested software products.
  • Route standards-related actions, including requests requiring Enterprise Software Board consideration for inclusion in the Technology Products Registry.
  • Submit software license evaluation requests to support licensing compliance prior to purchase and/or installation.
  • Support software request triage and routing based on request complexity, technology, dollar value, procurement approach, and other Government-defined criteria.
  • Coordinate software request activities with applicable software governance and vendor management organizations.

Software Entitlement and Asset Management:

  • Collect and document software entitlement information using the Software License Information Form (SLIF) and other required supporting documentation.
  • Maintain software intake and entitlement artifacts in Government-designated repositories.
  • Provide SLIFs and supporting entitlement documentation to Software Licensing Specialists for authoritative repository/database entry.
  • Support reconciliation of software entitlement information against software consumption or inventory data.
  • Identify discrepancies, exceptions, or incomplete information requiring further analysis or resolution.
  • Maintain traceable documentation and supporting evidence associated with software asset and entitlement activities.

Customer and Stakeholder Coordination:

  • Communicate with Government customers regarding software request status, requirements, funding needs, and outstanding actions.
  • Coordinate with Infrastructure, Enterprise Architecture, Software Administrators, Financial teams, acquisition stakeholders, and other support organizations.
  • Follow up on aging requests to ensure procurement, installation, Tier 2, or other responsible organizations are actively progressing assigned actions.
  • Collaborate with team members to share information, best practices, and lessons learned.
  • Support knowledge management and continuous improvement of software request and asset management processes.

Compensation and Benefits:

At NDi, we value our team and are committed to retaining top talent by offering competitive benefits and compensation packages. Our employee benefits package includes comprehensive health, dental, vision, pet, and legal insurance. Our corporate benefits include 401(k) retirement matching, paid leave, paid holidays, and health and wellness programs. In addition, we provide employer-paid life and disability insurance, professional development, education benefits, and much more to ensure our team has the resources they need to thrive on and off the job.

Veterans First Commitment:

As a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), NDi is dedicated to hiring veterans and providing a supportive work environment that honors their service while recognizing the unique skills and experiences they bring to our organization.

Our Commitment:

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

Apply Now: Take advantage of this unique opportunity to join one of the fastest-growing companies in Federal contracting!

title: Data Test Manager / Portfolio QA Lead
description:
Data Test Manager / Portfolio QA Lead

Location: Remote
Clearance Required: Active SC Clearance

Inside IR35

We are seeking an experienced Data Test Manager / Portfolio QA Lead to join a major data delivery programme. This is a strategic quality assurance role responsible for driving test governance, quality standards, and delivery assurance across a portfolio of large-scale data and analytics projects.

Working closely with Engagement Managers, Technical Leads, delivery teams, and key stakeholders, you will ensure testing best practices are consistently applied throughout the full software development lifecycle, from requirements through to implementation.

  • Review project scope, testing impacts, risks, and delivery approaches.
  • Lead QA recruitment activities and support capability development across the testing community.
  • Contribute to resource planning, forecasting, and allocation of QA resources.

Why Apply?

This is an opportunity to play a key leadership role, shaping testing standards and quality assurance across a portfolio of business-critical data projects. title: Administrative Coordinator
description:
Administrative Coordinator

Location: Xenia, Ohio – On-Site
Employment Type: Full-Time
Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
Pay Range: $20.00–$24.00 per hour
Annualized Range: $41,600–$49,920

Position Summary

Miami Valley Community Action Partnership (MVCAP) is seeking an organized, dependable, and service-oriented Administrative Coordinator to support the daily administrative and operational functions of our Greene County programs, including the Donnellan Shelter and related housing stability and supportive service programs.

The Administrative Coordinator plays an important role in keeping program operations organized and efficient. This position provides administrative support, assists with client screenings and referrals, processes invoices and purchase requests, maintains program and fiscal documentation, coordinates vendors and supplies, and supports the Greene County Director and program staff.

The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, comfortable managing multiple priorities, and able to communicate professionally with clients, staff, vendors, and community partners.

Key Responsibilities

Administrative & Program Support

  • Coordinate and support daily administrative operations for Greene County programs, including the Donnellan Shelter and housing stability programs.

  • Provide administrative support to the Greene County Director, Program Managers, Case Managers, and other program staff.

  • Maintain organized and accurate program records, files, reports, and supporting documentation.

  • Answer incoming telephone calls, emails, and general inquiries in a professional and timely manner.

  • Provide general program information and direct clients and community members to appropriate programs, resources, or staff.

  • Assist with correspondence, data entry, tracking, documentation, and other administrative functions.

Client Screening & Referral Coordination

  • Screen incoming calls and inquiries for shelter and housing stability programs, including the Homeless Crisis Response Program (HCRP).

  • Receive referrals from 211, community organizations, and partner agencies.

  • Complete applicable referral forms, screening tools, and preliminary program documentation.

  • Forward completed screening and referral information to appropriate program staff for eligibility determination and follow-up.

  • Maintain accurate records of referrals, screenings, and program inquiries.

  • Assist with communication between clients, program staff, and community partners while maintaining appropriate confidentiality.

Fiscal & Financial Support

  • Prepare and process purchase requisitions, invoices, billing documentation, and related fiscal paperwork.

  • Assist with administrative documentation for HCRP expenditures, including deposits, rental assistance, utility assistance, and other approved supportive services.

  • Monitor invoices and supporting documentation to assist with timely and accurate payment processing.

  • Track cash donations, in-kind contributions, supportive services, and other applicable program transactions.

  • Maintain fiscal documentation for program reporting, monitoring, and audit purposes.

  • Communicate with program leadership and Fiscal staff regarding missing documentation or discrepancies.

Purchasing, Vendors & Facility Support

  • Coordinate the ordering, tracking, and inventory of office and program supplies with appropriate approval.

  • Maintain purchasing, supply, and inventory records.

  • Coordinate scheduling and communication with approved vendors, maintenance providers, and service contractors.

  • Follow up on scheduled services and communicate facility or operational concerns to leadership.

Staff, Intern & Volunteer Support

  • Assist with onboarding and orientation activities for new staff, interns, students, and volunteers.

  • Support administrative coordination of volunteers, interns, and students assigned to Greene County programs.

  • Maintain required records and documentation as directed.

Qualifications

Required:

  • High School Diploma or General Equivalency Diploma (G.E.D.).

  • Minimum of two (2) years of experience in administrative support, office coordination, fiscal support, program support, or a related area.

  • Strong organizational, communication, customer service, and time-management skills.

  • Ability to maintain confidential and sensitive information with professionalism and discretion.

  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and Teams, as well as Adobe Acrobat.

Preferred:

  • Experience working in a nonprofit, housing, shelter, social services, or community action environment.

  • Familiarity with intake systems, databases, or comparable software applications.

  • Associate degree or higher in social services, business administration, office administration, or a related field.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Successful candidates should be able to:

  • Organize and prioritize multiple assignments in a fast-paced environment.

  • Maintain accurate records and documentation with strong attention to detail.

  • Communicate professionally and effectively, both verbally and in writing.

  • Provide quality customer service when interacting with clients, staff, and community partners.

  • Manage time-sensitive assignments while meeting deadlines.

  • Work independently while contributing effectively to a collaborative team.

  • Adapt to changing priorities, interruptions, and evolving program needs.

  • Maintain professionalism and confidentiality when handling client, employee, fiscal, and agency information.

Occasional local travel may be required to support agency business, program operations, or client-related needs.

Join MVCAP and help support programs that connect individuals and families with resources, services, and opportunities that promote stability and self-sufficiency.

Pre-hire: Mandatory drug testing and background check.

title: Manufacturing Engineering Development Program (MEDP) – US – January 2027 Start
description:
Job Description Summary

Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we believe the world works better when it flies. We are a world-leading provider of jet engines, components, and integrated systems for commercial and military aircraft. We have a relentless dedication to the future of safe and more sustainable flight and believe in our talented people to make it happen.

Job Description

Job Summary

The Manufacturing Engineering Development Program (MEDP) is a 2-year development program in manufacturing focused on developing and accelerating technical expertise across the Supply Chain. Engineers in the MEDP will work in manufacturing engineering assignments to gain experience through a mix of on-the-job training and classroom education structured to provide a foundation of technical and leadership skills. You'll complete two 12-month assignments to cultivate growth in key technical disciplines and engineering responsibilities. In addition, the MEDP will foster mentorship and structured learning opportunities with our team of manufacturing experts. Upon completion, you will be ready for promotional opportunities to further advance in GE Aerospace.

  • Utilize various design and analytical software to support and improve manufacturing processes.

  • Advance and develop manufacturing planning, processes and work instructions.

  • Work with cross-functional teams to identify and implement process improvements to improve product quality, increase throughput, and reduce manufacturing costs.

  • Collect and analyze data from manufacturing processes to drive short- and long-term actions that support production.

  • Apply Lean and Six Sigma tools to identify waste and support decision-making processes.

  • Manage project plans related to manufacturing changes and collaborate with various functions to drive action and project closure.

  • Focused: quick learner, strategically prioritizes work, committed, and takes initiative

title: Communications & Fibre Technicians
description:
Stowe Australia, one of Australia’s largest Electrical & Communications Contractors, is currently recruiting experienced Communications & Fibre Technicians to support a project in Adelaide.

This role will be employed from our Melbourne office and employed under a Victorian Enterprise Bargaining Agreement. (EBA)

Immediate starts are available, and applicants who can commence on short notice will be highly regarded.

Responsibilities:
  • Carry out fibre optic splicing, jointing, termination, testing and fault-finding works.
  • Prepare fibre optic cables for connector termination, including jacket stripping, buffer removal, fibre cleaning and strength-member preparation.
  • Terminate single mode and multimode fibre connectors using epoxy/resin-based hand-polish methods.
  • Complete connector assembly and fibre termination, including polishing and end-face finishing.
  • Pot connector ferrules and prepare fibre terminations for curing, polishing and inspection.
  • Carry out insertion loss testing using optical light source and power meter equipment.

Conduct continuity and fault checks using visual fault locators.

  • Perform OTDR testing where required by project specifications.
  • Test, troubleshoot and fault-find fibre optic networks to identify and rectify performance issues.

title: Fractional Data Privacy Specialist
description:
About us

At Jigsaw, we’re on a mission to transform the way professional services and financial institutions work. We do this by helping our clients organise, visualise and use their data (think Figma or Canva but for the ‘City’). Our clients include the world’s biggest consultancies, leading financial institutions and top law firms.

Jigsaw was founded by two seasoned entrepreneurs, Stephen and Travis. This is their second venture together; their first was acquired by a US private equity firm and went on to become a billion-dollar company and a household name in professional service firms across the world. Jigsaw is now on a growth trajectory few Series A companies achieve - putting us in the top quartile SaaS companies globally. Today we proudly serve thousands of users from nearly two hundred businesses worldwide, who love our products and use them everyday.

But we’re only getting started! We have ambitious goals and we’re looking for talented people to help us achieve them.

Why join us?

We're not about the corporate grind; instead, we thrive on creativity, enthusiasm, and a touch of humour to make magic happen.

We hire people with high ownership and a bias for action. Then we trust and empower them to do their best work.

About the role

You'll be Jigsaw's embedded data privacy advisor: the person product, engineering, and customer-facing teams turn to when a data or privacy question needs a real answer. This is a fractional role (starting at roughly 2 days a week in-office), working closely alongside our Legal Ops Associate.

The focus for this role will be translating legal and technical complexity into commercially-focused, actionable responses to help free up teams to move quickly. In practice, this could be advising the product team on what compliance actions we need to take ahead of a new product release, making case-by-case decisions for customers with unique compliance requirements, or conducting analysis on customer DPAs ahead of a change to data processing locations, right through to how to answer a client's questions about our AI features.

This isn't a standardise-everything-and-leave role. We work with customers around the world in regulated industries (legal, finance, accountancy, corporate) with varying compliance needs, where one-size-fits-all templates aren't always an option and we need to adopt a flexible approach. The work here is genuinely ongoing, nuanced, and advisory rather than a project with an end date.


You'll get to...

  • Act as the go-to person for data and privacy questions across the business - in product meetings, customer rollout calls, and migration conversations

  • Turn specific customer contract terms into practical, commercial recommendations, weighing real risk instead of defaulting to "no"

  • Advise on cross-border and international data transfer questions, which come up constantly given our global customer base

  • Join customer calls to speak credibly with clients' own data privacy counsel, many of whom are lawyers or privacy specialists themselves

  • Translate complex legal and technical concepts clearly for non-legal, technical teams internally

  • Help build a genuine "privacy by design" culture at Jigsaw - getting privacy thinking embedded at the start of projects, not bolted on at the end

  • Spot opportunities to improve our templates, playbooks, and processes proactively, alongside the day-to-day reactive work

You'll need...

  • A working understanding of UK & US privacy laws, including UK & EU GDPR, the UK Data Protection Act and CCPA, ideally with experience applying them in a live commercial context, not just in theory

  • Genuine on-the-ground experience inside a tech company building product - this isn't a fit for a purely private-practice legal background

  • To be genuinely comfortable with cross-border and international data transfer questions

  • To be a commercial, pragmatic, solution-minded operator - someone who can weigh the significance and likelihood of a risk and propose a workable path forward, not someone who leads with compliance-first blockers

  • Excellent communication skills on two levels: credible and precise with legally sophisticated clients, and clear and accessible for non-legal internal teams

  • High ownership balanced with genuine collaboration, and able to build consensus

  • Comfort with a fractional working pattern - broadly protected days, with the pragmatic flexibility to handle something urgent (like a data incident) outside them

Nice-to-haves

  • Familiarity with other privacy frameworks, including AI governance or AI-related compliance questions

  • CIPP/E or CIPM certification

  • Experience working with clients in heavily regulated industries (law firms, accountancies, financial services)

  • Prior experience at a similar-stage scale-up with a broad base of regulated, legally sophisticated customers

Who should apply?

If you find the letter-of-the-law side of privacy the least interesting part of the job, and you're energised instead by being commercial, pragmatic, and embedded in a fast-moving business — this is for you. You'll get real autonomy and visibility across the company, working directly with product, engineering, and customer teams, rather than being buried in reactive, box-ticking compliance work.

title: DSHS HCLA Budget Forecast Administrator
description:
Description

Budget Forecast Administrator: Home and Community Living Administration – Management Services Division

You will help shape how Washington invests in services that support people to live with greater choice, independence, and safety. As the Budget Forecast Administrator, you will bring together budget expertise, forecasting skills, sound judgment, and a practical understanding of how funding decisions affect programs and the people they serve.

This is a senior-level role with a broad view of the financial picture for two of the DSHS’ largest administrations: Home and Community Living Administration (HCLA) and the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA). Together, they manage a biennial budget of approximately $19.65 billion and more than 7,000 full-time equivalent staff. You will lead a team of 12 professional staff while working closely with executive leaders, program teams, the Office of Financial Management, legislative fiscal staff, the Caseload Forecast Council, and other state partners.

Every week brings something different as you move through Washington’s budget cycle. You may be helping an executive team understand funding needs, guiding a decision package, responding to questions about caseloads and expenditures, preparing a fiscal note, or helping a forecast team understand whether the numbers tell the right story. You will have room to chart a path for the team, improve how the work gets done, and build trusted relationships throughout state government.

Some of what you will do

  • Lead the development, submission, implementation, and monitoring of HCLA and DDA biennial and supplemental budgets, including decision packages, allotments, spending plans, and year-end projections.
  • Direct Medicaid caseload, per-capita, and expenditure forecasts for nursing home, in-home, community residential, waiver, and other services, using available data to identify trends, explain variances, and recommend adjustments.
  • Supervise, coach, and develop the professional staff, providing direction on complex assignments while creating an environment where people can ask questions, share ideas, and grow their skills.
  • Serve as a primary resource for executive leaders, program managers, the Central Budget Office, the Office of Financial Management, legislative fiscal staff, and other partners on budget, forecast, and funding questions.
  • Guide the preparation of fiscal notes, legislative budget requests, financial reports, and other materials that clearly explain the fiscal impact of proposed legislation, policies, and program changes.
  • Participate in the financial modeling for complex issues, such as Adult Family Home collective bargaining, by working with rates, labor relations, program, and budget teams to develop reliable fiscal estimates.
  • Oversee budget management, modeling, and reporting for the Washington Cares Fund and respond to changing legislative, program, and agency requirements.
  • Provide technical guidance and practical solutions on complex fiscal questions while looking for ways to make processes more efficient and help the team meet changing demands throughout the budget and forecasting cycles.

Fast forward one year

You have developed trusted working relationships with executive leaders, program teams, the Office of Financial Management, and legislative partners. You can confidently lead the decision package process, identify gaps and help teams determine how to address them, and guide the budget and forecast team through the demands of the state budget cycle. You understand HCLA and DDA programs and can connect funding needs to the services they provide. You have also identified opportunities to make the work more efficient and have begun putting your own ideas into practice.

Who should apply

You bring a combination of public-sector budget experience, financial expertise, leadership skills, and curiosity about how government funding supports services. We are looking for someone who can:

  • Lead complex budget development, forecasting, financial modeling, and expenditure projection work.
  • Supervise and develop professional staff while balancing independent decision-making with collaboration.
  • Interpret legislation, policies, regulations, financial reports, and other complex information and translate it into clear recommendations.
  • Communicate complex financial information clearly in writing and conversation with executives, staff, legislators, state agencies, and other partners.
  • Manage multiple priorities and deadlines, particularly during the fast-changing state budget cycle.
  • Research unfamiliar issues, ask thoughtful questions, and use sound judgment to develop practical solutions.
  • Build productive working relationships and remain patient, flexible, and constructive when priorities or circumstances change.
  • Use financial database software and business systems, including Microsoft Excel, at an advanced level.

Required qualifications: You have at least 10 years of professional experience in budget development, financial reporting, expenditure and revenue projections, and related financial practices. This experience must include at least 3 years supervising professional staff and a thorough understanding of Washington state’s financial environment. This includes experience using state financial systems related to budget, accounting, human resources, fiscal notes, bill tracking, or enterprise reporting.

A master’s degree in business, public administration, accounting, economics, statistics, or a related field may substitute for some of the required professional experience, consistent with the applicable job classification. A bachelor’s degree may also be considered with the corresponding additional professional experience.

Preferred experience includes legislative processes and fiscal notes, Medicaid or Medicare funding, long-term services and supports, grant funding, and HCLA or DDA programs. Experience working with Washington state government is also helpful, but DSHS experience is not required.

Work location

This is a hybrid role based in Lacey, with an expectation of working from the Lacey HCLA headquarters approximately two days each week. Occasional travel may be available to connect with staff and programs across the state.

DSHS partners with people to access support, care, and resources. This role is classified as Washington Management Services 3 (WMS3) and offers an opportunity to do more than manage numbers. You will help connect Washington’s resources with the services people rely on—and help a talented team find better ways to do that work.

Interested? Please list 3 professional references’ current contact information on your application and include your current resume and a letter of interest explaining how your knowledge, skills, and abilities qualify you for this role.

Questions? Please contact the Recruiter, Jenny, at bastrjl@dshs.wa.gov or 360-725-5810 and reference #06891. Learn more about DSHS.

The Department of Social and Health Services’ (DSHS) vision that people find human services to shape their own lives requires that we come together with a sense of belonging, common purpose, shared values, and meaningful work. We strive to support all Washingtonians, including Black, Indigenous, and People of Color, people with physical, behavioral health, and intellectual disabilities, elders, LGBTQIA+ individuals, immigrants and refugees, and families building financial security.

title: Late technical cofounder — Agentee
description:
Late technical cofounder — Agentee
Remote, anywhere · equity + a real-but-small base · English is enough The company
We don’t build chatbots or “AI tools.” We raise digital employees — Agentees. They’re onboarded like colleagues: simple work first, corrections, earned trust, then more scope. Humans stay on the four-eyes. Every action is logged. Alea already sits in finance, Claire in claims/CS, more coming. Live clients, not a deck. The product works. It’s still in baby shoes. Demand is huge. Delivery is the bottleneck. Who you’d partner with
Daniel Stojanovic — serial cofounder (Fintech, RecTech, now Agentic). Part of the fino group: ~200 people, our software in almost every German bank. He sells, maps the process, and holds the client. What’s missing is the person who makes the product side as ambitious as that. The opportunity
- Take a working Agentee platform and turn it into something that can 2× a year without adding headcount. Goal: stay under 10 people, do the work of a hundred, 10M valuation in 36 months.
- Own the technical and product seat at founder level: architecture, delivery, how we raise Agentees, how we ship. Co-decide hiring, stack, and what we refuse to build.
- Orchestrate a few humans and a lot of Agentees. Claude writes the syntax. You decide what gets built, what stays human, and when something is actually done. The role (week one, not week twelve)
- Own deploys and incidents from day one.
- Put structure around a product that’s grown by client fire — so we can grow, not just patch.
- Sit in the messy client reality (NAV, DATEV, Teams, mail) and turn it into something an Agentee can run. Architect, not ticket-dev. Who this is for
You’ve owned something end-to-end at a place small enough that your name was on the outage. The stack is Python. You barely write the lines yourself. No German required. Distributed, chaotic, direct, new clients every month. We work hard and we’ll still laugh at a dirty joke at 1am. If you need weekends off in writing, skip this. If you’ve always known you’re not the 9-to-5 version of yourself, and you haven’t had a place to prove it — this might be it. The deal
Meaningful shares (late cofounder, not employee options). We can’t pay a big salary yet. We’ll make sure you can pay rent. If we hold ~100% growth a year, salaries double with the company. Anywhere on earth. Write: hiring@agentee.io — a few lines on something you owned that almost broke you, and why this seat.

title: Health Promotion Specialist
description:
Description

Click HERE for Video

Who we are. We protect lives. The Georgia Department of Public Health is the lead agency entrusted by the people of Georgia to proudly protect lives and promote healthy lifestyles in diverse communities statewide. We are committed to preventing disease, injury, and disability; promoting health and well-being; and preparing the State of Georgia for responding to disasters.

What we offer. As a member of the Georgia Department of Public Health team, you will join a passionate group of individuals who are dedicated to making an impact. No matter your role, you will individually contribute to protecting the lives of all Georgians while receiving a wide range of benefits, so you can:

  • Make a Professional Impact – Build your career where it matters and protect lives in the community where you live, work, and play
  • Enjoy Workplace Flexibility – Experience flexibility in how you work so you can be your best self for you and Georgia Residents
  • Work with a Dynamic and Diverse Team– Collaborative and inclusive way of working where employees share ideas and leverage collective strengths
  • Achieve Career Longevity – Countless opportunities for continuous learning/development that support a long-term career
  • Take Part in a Hands-on Working Culture – Unique culture of active engagement and problem-solving, no matter your role
  • Feel Pride in Where you Work – Be part of making an impact in public health alongside dedicated people just like you

As a Health Promotion Specialist within the Columbus Health Department at the Georgia Department of Public Health, you will join a dedicated group of public health professionals that help support the overall mission and vision of protecting lives of Georgian residents in a variety of ways.

Job Responsibilities

This position will be housed in Columbus, GA and will assist with the development and implementation of health promotion programs within the 16 counties of the West Central Health District. You will support the Department by utilizing your expertise to fulfill the following responsibilities:

  • develop partnerships with faith-based communities, schools, work sites and the community at large and assist these groups with developing health promotion programs
  • prepare and disseminate educational and informational materials
  • promote health discussions within schools, industry, and community agencies
  • teach groups and/or individuals on health education/promotion topics
  • provide information to the public regarding health concerns and resources.

*This is Not a Remote position.

Minimum Qualifications

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Bachelor’s degree in education, social, behavioral, or biological sciences or a directly related field from an accredited college or university.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Bachelor’s and/or Master’s degree in Public Health from an accredited college or university, preferred. Must have effective verbal and written communication skills, such as oral presentations, written reports, articles, and data entry. Must be able to establish effective working relationships with internal and external partners, coalitions, and stakeholders. Knowledgeable in Excel, MS Word, and PowerPoint.

Additional Information

All West Central Health District 7 employees are deemed essential workers in the event of an emergency. As such, you may be called on to participate in an event including but not limited to: staffing a shelter, working at a Specimen Point of Collection Site (SPOC) and/or working at a Point of Dispensing site (POD). If you are called on to participate, you are required to report to the designated site as a condition of employment, whether the emergency occurs during or outside regular work hours.

Georgia Department of Public Health Commissioner and leaders encourages all employees to engage in regular physical activities and to make lifestyle choices that promote health and well-being. The use of physical breaks during the workday is authorized to support this philosophy and assist employees in meeting their physical goals. A maximum of 30 minutes in a given workday may be used to engage in physical activities, generally in the form of two 15-minute breaks or one 30-minute break.

Employment Information

DPH accepts educational credential recognized by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) and/or the US Department of Education (DOE) will be considered. DPH will contact educational institutions to verify degree, diploma, licensure, etc.

The candidate selected for this position may be subject to pre-employment drug screening and a criminal background check.

As an employee of DPH, in the event of an identified emergency you may be required, as a term and condition of employment, to assist in meeting the emergency responsibilities of the department.

At Booker, along with being a great place to work and giving you an opportunity to get on in your career, we also offer the following fantastic package of benefits:

  • After 3 months service, a Tesco colleague discount card with 10% increasing to 15% off most purchases at Tesco for a 4 day period after every four-weekly pay day, ie. thirteen times a year. In addition to 10% off at Tesco Cafe and 20% off all F&F purchases.

About the role

As a Software Development Engineer, you’ll help design, build and support resilient back-office systems that power sales, stock control and financial accuracy across our Booker estate. You’ll work across a mixed technology landscape—combining legacy systems with modern platforms—to deliver reliable, scalable solutions for high-volume wholesale operations.

This is a 12-month fixed-term opportunity where you’ll play a key role in maintaining system performance, delivering change safely, and supporting business-critical services. You’ll collaborate closely with colleagues across Technology, Operations, and external partners to ensure everything we release is robust, secure and ready for real-world use.

You will be responsible for

  • Design, develop and maintain store back-office systems using COBOL, Java, REST APIs and scripting within a Linux environment
  • Deliver high-quality, well-tested code aligned with engineering standards and change control processes
  • Support and enhance system functionality to ensure accuracy, resilience and performance—especially around stock integrity and sales processing
  • Diagnose and resolve complex technical issues, providing 3rd line support and identifying long-term fixes
  • Deliver system changes, upgrades and new store rollouts with minimal disruption to trading
  • Collaborate with product, programme teams, operations and third-party suppliers to deliver effective solutions
  • Produce and maintain clear technical documentation covering design, interfaces and support processes
  • Ensure systems meet security, audit and compliance requirements
  • Continuously improve system performance and maintainability, supporting modernisation while maintaining legacy systems
  • Contribute to team learning, peer reviews and continuous improvement of development practices

You will need

You will need

  • Proven experience delivering and supporting business-critical software in a production environment
  • Hands-on experience with COBOL and Java, or a strong willingness to work across both
  • Experience working in a Linux environment, including scripting and batch processing
  • Knowledge of transactional or back-office systems (e.g. stock control, sales processing, financial systems), ideally in retail or wholesale
  • Strong problem-solving skills, with experience diagnosing and resolving complex live issues
  • Experience delivering changes via structured development and release processes
  • Familiarity with source control tools like Git and development lifecycle practices
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills, working with technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Ability to produce clear technical documentation
  • Awareness of security, governance and compliance requirements

About The Company

Booker is the UK's leading food & drink wholesaler. We are privileged to serve independent retailers, caterers and small businesses, from locations across the country. We operate over 190 cash and carry branches, eight distribution centres, five Best Food Logistics sites, as well as six support centre locations across the UK.

title: Research & Development Chemist
description:
About Us

Dulux Acratex is a market leader in high-performance texture coatings, façade systems, and roofing solutions, designed to protect and beautify the Australian built environment. From iconic heritage restorations to cutting-edge residential and commercial projects, we deliver style, durability, and sustainability that stand the test of time.

As part of DuluxGroup, we offer a culture of innovation, collaboration, and growth. Our people enjoy world-class training, career pathways, and benefits like flexible work options and generous parental leave. Join us and help shape iconic spaces while building a rewarding career in a team that values creativity and excellence.


What You'll Be Doing

As a Research & Development Chemist, you'll help develop the next generation of coating technologies that support Acratex's market-leading position. This is a hands-on R&D role where you'll be actively involved in formulation, testing and product development, working closely with experienced scientists and cross-functional teams to turn ideas into commercially successful products.

Initially, the role will focus on cementitious render products, with opportunities to expand into other coating technologies as your experience and development grow. You'll improve existing formulations, contribute to new product innovations, solve technical challenges, and help deliver high-quality, sustainable solutions for customers. If you enjoy rolling up your sleeves, getting your hands dirty, and seeing your work come to life in real-world applications, this role is for you.


Our Benefits

  • Up to $1,000 net annually to cover private health extras gap costs
  • Exclusive discounts on DuluxGroup products and partner offers
  • Stay active anytime, anywhere through our partnership with Fitness Passport
  • 20 weeks paid parental leave (primary carers) and 2 weeks partner leave from day one
  • Market-leading learning, development and career pathways
  • Access to our Wellbeing Hub and full EAP support
  • Recognition programs that celebrate your impact


What We're Looking For

  • Degree qualifications in Chemistry, Applied Science or a related STEM discipline
  • Formulation experience, ideally within coatings, paints or related industries
  • Strong analytical skills with experience interpreting and leveraging data insights
  • Proven problem-solving capability and a structured approach to root cause analysis
  • Excellent communication, influencing and stakeholder management skills
  • Highly organised, detail-oriented and committed to quality outcomes
  • Collaborative team player with the ability to work autonomously and manage competing priorities
  • Growth mindset with a passion for continuous learning and innovation
  • Drive to develop market-leading products and deliver commercially successful outcome


Why Join Us?

Progressing your career with DuluxGroup means being part of a network of over 8,000 employees globally who believe in our purpose to "Imagine a Better Place".

With origins dating back to 1918, we are a leading marketer and manufacturer of iconic brands including Dulux, Selleys, Cabot's, Yates and B&D.

By joining us, you'll be part of a long-term strategy focused on delivering profitable growth through brand leadership, innovation and customer intimacy. We're committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspectives are valued, while providing opportunities for career growth, internal mobility and flexible work options.

If this sounds like an opportunity, you'd like to be part of, we'd love to hear from you. Apply online today.

title: Software Engineer | Internship | Summer '27
description:
About BlockTech

BlockTech is a fast-paced algorithmic market maker facilitating global derivatives and spot trading, originating from crypto markets and expanding into new markets.

We trade our own capital on systems that run 24/7 and have to be fast and correct without exception. Our systems run on Linux and are written in Rust and Python.

For the Summer of 2027, we're looking for Software Engineer Interns to join our engineering team in Singapore.

The role

This is an 8-10 week summer internship at our Singapore office, giving you a unique opportunity to work on an end-to-end project with a real and direct business impact. You'll work in a small team and get the chance to understand how a trading firm actually works from the inside.

You will:

  • Participate in a customized training program that will give you an understanding of financial markets in general, the company, and the project.

  • Own a project from design to deployment, guided by experienced software engineers.

  • Work with production-level data and systems.

  • Learn from experienced engineers, traders, and researchers, and see how their work fits together.

What we're looking for

  • Currently in your (pen)ultimate year studying computer science or a related discipline at a top university in Singapore

  • Available full-time in Singapore for a duration of 8-10 weeks over the summer of 2027, starting on the 5th of July

  • Proficiency in a systems language (ideally Rust and/or C++) and working knowledge of Python

  • A solid grasp of data structures, algorithms, and what actually makes code fast

  • A critical mind that follows things until completion, high ownership, and clear communication in English

What's in it for you?

  • A summer internship in a relaxed and modern office in the heart of Singapore's financial district (CBD)

  • A dedicated mentor, a team of fellow interns and full-time software engineers, an in-house training program, and exposure to how engineering, research, and trading actually work together

  • The opportunity to work at the forefront of automated trading using technology built for speed and precision, in an environment that embraces AI to both accelerate productivity and advance our systems and models

  • Daily breakfast and warm lunch, snacks and drinks provided throughout the day, and regular socials and celebrations

  • The opportunity to convert into a full-time role after graduation, based on performance

Our culture

At our core, we are a team of passionate trading and tech enthusiasts committed to revolutionizing trading through automation. Our collaborative approach ensures that everyone contributes to achieving our ambitious goals.

In this role, you will be both challenged and stretched, with ample opportunities for growth and development, both within and beyond your main responsibilities.

We invest in our people by offering competitive compensation and benefits, fostering innovation, and celebrating success. Our commitment to personal development transcends traditional norms; we provide an equal playing field, promote reverse leadership, and offer boundless growth opportunities for all our employees.

Join us to unlock your potential and drive innovation in the exciting world of algorithmic trading.

title: Junior AI developer
description:
Take the first step in your technical career as a Junior AI Developer, working with experienced consultants to build practical AI solutions for clients across the public and private sectors.

Junior AI Developer

Home working, with requirements to work in the office in Birmingham City Centre a couple of times a month as requested

  • £25,000 per annum
  • Monday to Friday, 8.30am–5.00pm
  • Some flexibility when on site

About Our Client

This is a great opportunity for someone with experience in AI and data handling who is looking to take the first step in their technical career. Our client is experiencing strong growth, which offers exciting and varied opportunities for the right candidate to grow and progress within the company.

Our client is looking for a curious, ambitious Junior AI Developer to join its growing AI team.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone who has recently graduated in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Data Science or a related subject, and who is genuinely excited about how AI can solve real business problems.

You don’t need years of experience. What matters most is that you have a strong technical foundation, a willingness to learn and a genuine interest in AI that extends beyond your university studies.

About the Role

You’ll work alongside our client’s experienced AI consultants, helping to design, develop and deliver AI solutions for clients across a range of industries in both the public and private sectors.

You’ll learn how to take AI from an interesting idea to something that delivers measurable value for a business.

What You’ll Be Doing

Working closely with our client’s experienced consultants, you’ll have the opportunity to:

  • Understand client challenges and explore where AI can make a genuine difference.
  • Research and evaluate emerging AI and machine learning technologies.
  • Help design AI solutions, from initial ideas through to implementation, while keeping data protection and compliance in mind.
  • Build prototypes, proof-of-concepts and demonstrations.
  • Work with technologies such as generative AI, LLMs, Python, APIs and data.
  • Assist with prompt engineering, AI workflows and AI-powered applications.
  • Analyse data and help evaluate the performance and usefulness of AI solutions.
  • Support client workshops and presentations.
  • Document technical approaches and communicate findings clearly.
  • Learn to assess AI solutions for accuracy, privacy, security, fairness and responsible use.
  • Learn from senior consultants and gradually take ownership of your own areas of work.

What Our Client Is Looking For

You might be a great fit if you:

  • Have recently graduated, or are about to graduate, in AI, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Data Science or a related degree.
  • Have a good understanding of core AI and Machine Learning concepts, including Large Language Models (LLMs).
  • Have demonstrable practical experience using Git, Python and SQL: you have used them in university, personal or commercial projects and can talk our client through what you built.
  • Have experimented with AI or machine learning outside your university coursework.
  • Have kept up with developments in AI and enjoy exploring new tools and technologies.
  • Have built personal projects, experimented with LLMs, entered hackathons, contributed to GitHub projects or simply spent your spare time figuring out what AI can do.
  • Are naturally curious and enjoy solving problems.
  • Can explain technical concepts clearly to people who may not have a technical background.
  • Are comfortable working as part of a team and learning from more experienced people.
  • Are interested not just in how AI works, but in how businesses can use it effectively.
  • Desirable: You have been exposed to one or more of PostgreSQL, Linux, Java, JavaScript, APIs or Cloud Computing (Azure, GCP).

You don't need to know everything

This is a junior role, and our client doesn’t expect you to arrive as an AI expert.

Our client is looking for someone with the fundamentals, enthusiasm and curiosity to develop into an excellent AI Developer and Consultant.

Benefits

  • 25 days’ holiday, plus Bank Holidays.
  • Pension.
  • Private healthcare after successful completion of the probationary period.
  • Death in service scheme after successful completion of the probationary period.
  • Great career development and training opportunities.

How to Apply

If you have a strong technical foundation, a genuine interest in artificial intelligence and the curiosity to explore how it can solve real business problems, click “apply” today and check your inbox for an email providing more information on how to tailor your application and provide a cover letter or any supporting documents.

This role may also suit candidates with experience as a: Graduate AI Developer, Junior Machine Learning Engineer, Graduate Software Developer, Junior Data Scientist, AI Engineer, Machine Learning Developer, Python Developer, Generative AI Developer or AI Consultant.

title: Quality Technician
description:
Basic Function

The Quality Technician is responsible for the daily functions of maintaining high standards in the production process. They utilize their skills and knowledge to inspect products or processes, ensuring to meet predefined specifications and institute improvements as required.

Must effectively carry out the essential duties and responsibilities of this position to consistently promote our Mission, Vision and Values. Essential Duties and Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Balance Safety, Quality, Production, Cost and Morale to achieve positive results across departments.
  • Continuously learn, share, and implement corrections or changes to encourage organizational improvements for the department and company.
  • Use the 5s Pillars, Sort (Seiri), Set in Order (Seiton), Shine (Seiso), Standardize (Seiketsu), and sustain (Shitsuke) to maintain a clean and organized workspace to sustain a productive work environment.
  • Maintain the measuring equipment including both calibration and verification of accuracy.
  • Administer Education as needed and document within the department.
  • Maintain Daily Check Sheets and File Paperwork
  • Administer Final Approval of Incoming Logs
  • Conduct Billet Etches and provide approval to proceed with the process or notify supervisor when product is out of standard.
  • Conduct the Forge First Part Check when the forge is started and when the die is changed.
  • Measure the flash extension after trim to ensure accuracy.
  • Administer the Tensile Testing process to ensure that the integrity of the part is in good condition.
  • Approve Heat Treat Baskets based on test results from the Tensile Testing process to allow the parts to move to the next phase of production.
  • Conduct CMM Check on the parts after the Dye Pen process is completed.
  • Maintain Scrap Log and Hold Cage
  • Production Defect Support (Judgement Calls)

  • Measure the parts of a prototype trial when it is made

  • Other duties as assigned.

The employee is required to reach with hands and arms, climb stairs, balance, stoop, kneel, and crouch. The employee must be able to speak and hear and must occasionally lift or move up to 15 pounds.
  • The employee may enter the non-climate-controlled plant or warehouse where temperatures can be extremely hot or cold depending on the weather.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

Job Description

Your Role

Responsible for coordinating the work of HNE employees and assuring work is performed in compliance with regulatory and quality requirements.

This will be a first shift position.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Ensures all lines have appropriate labor to meet expectations and manages MAR operator assignments

  • Maintains contact with customer departments to ensure awareness of any product or process problems that affect customer satisfaction.

  • Leads initiatives to maintain a continuous improvement environment in Manufacturing operations. This includes implementing and innovating with six sigma, lean manufacturing, VSMs, 6’s, and other philosophies. These efforts aim to reduce waste and improve efficiency, quality, and safety.

  • Controls production shift schedule and works with support departments to set up actions when they are not achieved.

  • Identifies, communicate and work on issues in good timing to avoid impact in production schedule and/or operations

  • Assigns workers to workstations to meet production requirements and ensures specifications, GMP’s and GDP’s are followed. In depth knowledge of manufacturing systems, operations and work centers.

  • Follows quality procedures to identify and address Regulatory and Operational issues. Documents and records regulatory requirements in the Batch folder (parameters, test, verifications, etc)

  • Monitors production and adjusts work assignments, supply of material, and machine operation when necessary. Optimizes product and material flow to meet daily build plan.

  • Assist in updating procedures for process according to regulations, internal and corporate procedures and Baxter specifications and policies.

  • Enforces company policies for workers and enforces safety regulations.

  • Maintains an appropriate labor-management relationship with subordinates. Shows respect and sensitivity for cultural differences; promotes a harassment-free environment.

  • Ensures GMP's, GDP's and any EHS requirement are followed in areas of responsibility.

  • Assist root cause analysis and investigations to address safety, quality and/or productivity issues.

What You'll Bring

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills. Knowledge of corporate specifications and plant standard operating procedures. Knowledge of Bill of Material process. Must have good documentation practices, and strong interpersonal skills.Ability to pass visual acuity test (20/20 corrected vision) and pass Particulate Matter Certification

  • High school diploma required and experience, consistent with department process/product requirements.

  • Prior experience with mechanical, electrical equipment, and troubleshooting problems.

We understand compensation is an important factor as you consider the next step in your career. At Baxter, we are committed to equitable pay for all employees, and we strive to be more transparent with our pay practices. The pay for this role will be $30.50 per hour. For questions about this, our pay philosophy, and available benefits, please speak to the recruiter if you decide to apply and are selected for an interview.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

US Benefits at Baxter (except for Puerto Rico)

This is where your well-being matters. Baxter offers comprehensive compensation and benefits packages for eligible roles. Our health and well-being benefits include medical and dental coverage that start on day one, as well as insurance coverage for basic life, accident, short-term and long-term disability, and business travel accident insurance. Financial and retirement benefits include the Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), with the ability to purchase company stock at a discount, and the 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan (RSP), with options for employee contributions and company matching. We also offer Flexible Spending Accounts, educational assistance programs, and time-off benefits such as paid holidays, paid time off ranging from 20 to 35 days based on length of service, family and medical leaves of absence, and paid parental leave. Additional benefits include commuting benefits, the Employee Discount Program, the Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and childcare benefits. Join us and enjoy the competitive compensation and benefits we offer to our employees. For additional information regarding Baxter US Benefits, please speak with your recruiter or visit our Benefits site: Benefits | Baxter

Baxter is an equal opportunity employer. Baxter evaluates qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, protected veteran status, disability/handicap status or any other legally protected characteristic.

Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal

If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application or interview process, please click on the link here and let us know the nature of your request along with your contact information.
