description:
Position Title: AVP Special Assets

REPORTS TO: Chief Lending Officer

JOB STATUS: Exempt

JOB GRADE 16: $102,856.00 - $128.564.80 Targeted Annual Salary

JOB SUMMARY:

Reporting to the Chief Lending Officer, the AVP of Special Assets manages troubled and higher-risk commercial loans after they are transferred to Special Assets. The role works directly with borrowers and guarantors to develop practical plans to restore repayment when possible, restructure loans when appropriate, or recover as much as reasonably possible through collateral or legal remedies. The position also monitors credit risk, keeps leadership informed, and works closely with Commercial Lending, Credit Administration, Finance/Accounting, Legal Counsel, and Compliance to protect the Credit Union and support safe and sound lending.

Further, the position administers commercial watch-list, individually evaluated loans, and special-assets reporting and provides timely, accurate, and well-supported information regarding asset quality, risk-rating migration, delinquencies, nonaccruals, modifications, charge-offs, recoveries, collateral exposure, and workout progress. The AVP of Special Assets promotes safe and sound commercial lending practices consistent with applicable Credit Union policy, New Mexico law, NCUA regulations and supervisory guidance, and generally accepted accounting principles.

All employees of State Employees Credit Union are proactive, results driven, and fully committed to the Credit Union's mission and vision. They strive to achieve the highest standards of excellence and consistently exceed the expectations established by Credit Union Management.

Key Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Manage assigned problem commercial loans, including criticized/classified, individually evaluated loans, delinquent, nonaccrual, modified, and other higher-risk credits, from transfer to Special Assets through final resolution.
  • Monitor for changes in payment performance, financial condition, covenant compliance, collateral, bankruptcy, litigation, or other issues that increase risk, and adjust the action plan as needed.
  • Analyze borrower and guarantor financial information, repayment ability, cash flow, collateral, and other sources of support; recommend appropriate risk ratings and escalate material deterioration.
  • Exercise delegated authority within approved limits and obtain the appropriate approval for modifications, settlements, charge-offs, collateral releases, legal actions, and other material workout decisions.
  • Own and document the resolution strategy for assigned loans, including repayment sources, required actions, borrower and guarantor communication, responsible parties, approvals, milestones, deadlines, and target resolution dates. Periodically evaluate and adjust the strategy based on performance, risk, cost, and expected recovery.
  • Monitor workout and acquired-property expenses, protective advances, environmental exposure, vendor performance, and disposition timelines. Verify the accuracy of loan-system coding and regulatory reporting for assigned credits.
  • Make recommendations on nonaccrual status, return to accrual, charge-offs, and recoveries. Provide Finance/Accounting and Credit Administration with current information needed for CECL and allowance estimates.
  • Maintain the commercial watch list and provide clear, timely reporting on problem loans, risk changes, losses, recoveries, collateral shortfalls, and progress toward resolution.
  • Protect the Credit Union's collateral position by coordinating appraisals or evaluations, inspections, lien and title work, insurance, taxes, and other needed collateral-protection steps.
  • Work with Legal Counsel on bankruptcy, foreclosure, repossession, settlements, guarantor enforcement, collateral liquidation, and other legal remedies when needed.
  • Manage acquired commercial real estate or other collateral, including appropriate exit strategies, carrying costs, insurance, taxes, maintenance, environmental exposure, valuation, and disposition timelines.
  • Coordinate and oversee outside professionals such as attorneys, appraisers, brokers, receivers, auctioneers, or property managers when applicable.
  • Present problem credits and recommendations to the Loss Mitigation Committee and other leadership groups as needed; support audits, loan reviews, and examinations and maintain clear files supporting material decisions.
  • Follow Credit Union policy, delegated authority, applicable accounting requirements, and federal and New Mexico laws and regulations. Escalate suspected fraud, compliance concerns, or other significant issues and recommend improvements based on lessons learned.
  • Protect confidential information and follow applicable privacy, information-security, records-retention, and access-control requirements.
  • Complete required compliance, safety, security, and job-specific training within established timeframes.
  • Perform other duties as assigned

Required Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:

  • Advanced knowledge of commercial lending, credit analysis, credit administration, loan documentation, collections, and problem-loan resolution.
  • Ability to analyze commercial financial statements, tax returns, cash flow, repayment capacity, leverage, liquidity, collateral coverage, borrowing bases, and guarantor strength.
  • Practical knowledge of commercial risk ratings, nonaccrual treatment, CECL/allowance concepts, collateral evaluation, and the documentation needed to support credit decisions.
  • Working knowledge of bankruptcy, foreclosure, repossession, collateral liquidation, guarantor enforcement, and settlements, including knowing when legal counsel is needed.
  • Excellent negotiation, judgment, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to balance rehabilitation opportunities against loss exposure, time, cost, and likelihood of recovery.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to explain complex credit issues clearly to borrowers, management, committees, auditors, counsel, and regulators.
  • Strong organization and project-management skills with the ability to manage multiple complex credits, vendors, legal matters, deadlines, and competing priorities.

title: AIS ISC Demand Planning, Senior Director
description:
Job Description Summary

The AIS ISC Demand Planning Senior Director serves as the enterprise leader for Demand Planning and Integrated Business Planning (IBP), responsible for creating a connected planning environment that links business strategy, market demand, financial commitments, and operational execution across AIS. This role establishes the governance, operating framework, and planning architecture required to align executive decisions to enterprise priorities and business outcomes.

As a key member of the Planning Integrated Supply Chain leadership team, the Senior Director drives enterprise-wide planning effectiveness by ensuring a common view of demand, risks, opportunities, and strategic trade-offs. The role partners closely with Commercial, Finance, Operations, Product Management, and Supply Chain leaders to improve forecast accuracy, increase organizational agility, and enable informed decision-making that balances growth, customer outcomes, profitability, inventory, and cash flow.

This leader will champion the evolution of planning practices, capabilities, and technologies, advancing AIS toward a more predictive, insight-driven, and digitally enabled planning ecosystem.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Demand Planning & Integrated Planning Leadership

  • Define the strategic vision, governance model, and operating framework for Demand Planning and Integrated Business Planning across AIS.

  • Establish enterprise planning principles, standards, and performance expectations that drive consistency, transparency, and accountability across regions, business units, and functions.

  • Ensure alignment of long-range strategic plans, annual operating plans, demand forecasts, and execution priorities through an integrated planning approach.

  • Drive enterprise adoption of planning disciplines that support proactive decision-making and business performance management.

  • Serve as the senior advisor to executive leadership on demand, market trends, planning risks, and business implications.

Executive Business Performance & Decision Support

  • Lead executive planning reviews that facilitate timely decisions on business priorities, capacity, inventory, investment, and customer commitments.

  • Translate demand, supply, financial, and market signals into actionable insights and strategic recommendations for executive leadership.

  • Develop scenario planning and risk assessment processes that allow leaders to evaluate trade-offs and make informed decisions under uncertainty.

  • Enable greater visibility to business performance drivers and emerging risks through data-based planning intelligence and reporting.

Enterprise Forecasting & Demand Excellence

  • Lead the development of an integrated demand planning strategy that improves forecast quality, responsiveness, and organizational alignment.

  • Drive alignment around a single demand signal by integrating commercial inputs, market intelligence, customer trends, and operational constraints.

  • Establish key performance indicators, governance mechanisms, and management routines that improve planning effectiveness and forecast performance.

  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement through structured analysis of forecast performance, assumptions, and planning outcomes.

Financial & Strategic Alignment

  • Partner closely with Finance leadership to ensure demand plans support revenue, margin, inventory, and cash flow objectives.

  • Strengthen the connection between operational plans and financial commitments by improving planning transparency and business accountability.

  • Enable enterprise evaluation of growth opportunities, supply constraints, and investment decisions through integrated scenario analysis.

  • Ensure planning processes support strategic priorities while balancing short-term performance objectives and long-term business goals.

Planning Transformation & Digital Innovation

  • Lead the modernization of planning processes through advanced analytics, automation, artificial intelligence, and digital planning technologies.

  • Establish a multi-year roadmap that advances planning maturity and improves organizational responsiveness to changing market conditions.

  • Drive adoption of predictive insights and enhanced planning tools to improve decision quality and speed.

  • Partner with Digital and Analytics teams to strengthen planning data quality, visibility, and enterprise reporting capabilities.

Cross-Functional Enterprise Leadership

  • Build strong partnerships across Commercial, Operations, Finance, Product Management, Manufacturing, Fulfillment, and Supply Chain organizations.

  • Drive alignment to common assumptions, priorities, and measures of success across the enterprise.

  • Influence leaders at all levels to adopt standardized planning practices and enterprise-first decision making.

  • Foster collaboration across global teams to improve planning integration, performance, and execution.

Talent & Organizational Leadership

  • Lead and develop a high-performing global team responsible for enterprise demand planning and planning excellence.

  • Dotted line leadership for demand planning leaders across the AIS sub-segments

  • Build organizational strength through succession planning, leadership development, and capability enhancement.

  • Create an environment that encourages innovation, accountability, analytical thinking, and continuous learning.

  • Serve as a champion for enterprise planning excellence and operational rigor across AIS.

Qualifications & Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s/MBA preferred

  • Demonstrated experience in supply chain, planning, finance, or operations in a global organization

  • Deep expertise in IBP, S&OE, and integrated planning, with experience building and scaling enterprise capabilities

  • Proven experience leading and developing global teams, including leaders of leaders, with accountability for performance, capability building, and scaling organizational effectiveness across regions and functions

  • Proven experience leading enterprise transformation initiatives, including systems, analytics, and process standardization

  • Demonstrated ability to influence executive leadership and drive enterprise-wide alignment without direct authority

  • Strong business and financial acumen, with experience linking operational plans to financial outcomes

  • Track record of improving enterprise performance (OTD, inventory, forecast accuracy, working capital) through capability building

  • Experience embedding Lean, governance, and operating disciplines at scale

  • Healthcare or regulated industry experience preferred

title: Senior eCommerce & Optimisation Specialist
description:
24th August, 2026

We’re wrapped to be exclusively partnering with a truly iconic eCom brand on one very juicy new gig.

Global reach. Cult-level love. A reputation as fabulous as the brand itself.

Say hello to Blue Bungalow ✨

And this time? We’re after a seriously killer Senior eCommerce & Optimisation Specialist to join the crew and own eCommerce + optimisation excellence across their Shopify ecosystem.

This is one for the Shopify power users.

The humans who love getting under the hood of an eCommerce website. Who geek out on CRO, UX, CX and human behaviour. Who want to know why customers are dropping, where they’re getting stuck and how to make the experience perform even better.

And there’s plenty here to sink your teeth into.

Thousands of products. 70+ collections. Proper eCommerce complexity. An app already driving meaningful revenue with loads of opportunity to evolve and scale. And genuine ownership to help shape what comes next.

So if Shopify is your happy place…
If CRO, UX and understanding how humans actually shop online lights you up…
And if continually making a brilliant eCommerce experience even better sounds like your kinda gig…

This one might just be your vibe ✨

So… who is Blue Bungalow?

Born in Queensland in 2012, Blue Bungalow started as a love letter to the sun-drenched, beachside lifestyle, bringing a little slice of Queensland to women everywhere.

What began as a curated edit of kaftans and coastal essentials has grown into a globally loved fashion destination, now home to thousands of styles and over 150 brands, worn across Australia, New Zealand, the US and beyond.

Adored for their deeply personal, customer-first approach and powered by smart digital + tech innovation, Blue Bungalow is an ever-evolving brand with real heart. Behind it all? A deeply talented team of creative, digital and eCommerce minds building the next chapter with intention, innovation and unmistakable flair.

THE GIG

As the Senior eCommerce & Optimisation Specialist, you’ll become the go-to human for Shopify, website performance and optimisation across Blue Bungalow’s eCommerce world.

Reporting into a truly killer Head of Digital & eCommerce, and working closely with the Head of Creative + an epic eCommerce crew, you’ll sit right at the heart of how the online experience performs, evolves and grows.

You’ll also have a fab Senior eCommerce Coordinator reporting into you, helping keep the eCommerce Ops + customer side humming while you own the deeper Shopify, technical + optimisation piece.

And while there’s some lovely leadership baked in, this is still very much a hands-on senior specialist role. The really juicy bit? Understanding how humans actually shop.

Where are customers dropping? What’s getting in their way? Could navigation be smarter? Is creative helping them convert? What’s happening through cart and checkout? You’ll connect the dots across CRO, UX, CX, customer behaviour and commercial performance, then turn those insights into action.

You’ll become the anchor between eCommerce, Creative, CRM, CX and Development, bringing together what customers are saying, what the data is showing and what the wider team is seeing to make smarter decisions onsite.
You definitely don’t need to be a developer, but you’ll have enough technical chops to troubleshoot, understand what’s happening under the hood and know when to bring in Blue Bungalow’s Shopify development partner, briefing and QA’ing their work with confidence.

And then there’s the app. Already driving meaningful revenue, there’s a huge opportunity to build out app-specific features and make it an even stronger part of the eCommerce mix. You’ll be trusted to spot opportunities, bring ideas to the table and help shape what Blue Bungalow tackles next.

AND YOU?

First things first, you know Shopify properly.

You might already be an eCommerce, Optimisation, Website or Shopify legend brand-side. Or perhaps you’re agency or consultancy-side, owning Shopify, eCommerce or digital experience roadmaps, working closely with experience teams and developers, and fancy getting your hands on one brilliant eCommerce ecosystem to make your own.

Either way, you’ve actually been in the work. You understand how all the moving parts of an eCommerce website fit together and have a deep obsession with making it better.

YOUR DAY WILL LOOK A LIL’ LIKE THIS…

  • Own the day-to-day health, performance + optimisation of Shopify.
  • Make the customer journey better across landing pages, collections, products, cart + checkout.
  • Dig into conversion, funnel drop-off + customer behaviour to find those juicy optimisation opportunities.
  • Shape + run CRO experiments and A/B tests, turning insight into action and measuring what worked.
  • Make navigation, merchandising, product discovery + UX smarter across a pretty sizeable catalogue.
  • Troubleshoot themes, apps + integrations, tackling what you can and bringing in the dev experts when you need them.
  • Brief, manage + QA Blue Bungalow’s Shopify development partner across bigger builds + improvements.
  • Connect the dots across eCommerce, Creative, CRM + CX to make smarter onsite decisions.
  • Help evolve + scale the mobile app, creating an experience that goes well beyond simply mirroring the website.
  • Bring ideas + priorities to the table and help shape what happens next across the wider eCommerce roadmap.
THE GOOD STUFF YOU’LL BRING
  • Genuine, hands-on Shopify / Shopify Plus depth. This is the biggie.
  • A proper love for CRO, UX, CX + human behaviour, with real examples of where you’ve personally made an eCommerce experience better.
  • You know your numbers, with confidence across conversion, funnels + experimentation and tools like GA4 + Shopify Analytics firmly in your wheelhouse.
  • Enough technical chops to get amongst themes, apps + integrations and work beautifully with developers, while still seeing the bigger eCommerce picture.
  • Proper commercial instincts + an appreciation for great creative. You get how customer behaviour, creative, website decisions, product performance + revenue all play together.
  • Curiosity, autonomy + a little leadership sparkle. You’re happy steering the ship and guiding others, but still love being close to the work.
And if you know your way around eCommerce tools + products like Tapcart, Braze, Tagalys, Matrixify, Refundid and Shop Pay, or similar tech, even better. You don’t need every logo on your CV, but you’ll understand where they sit, how they connect and the role they play in a cracking eCommerce ecosystem.

A little Liquid literacy will come in super handy for this one too.

Bring us that Senior eCommerce brain, technical curiosity + love for optimisation, and the rest can absolutely be learned.

SOUND LIKE A BIT OF YOU?

title: Strategic Product Director ICP/OES (Washington State)
description:
The Company

PerkinElmer is a global analytical services and solutions provider with offerings including the leading OneSource Field and Laboratory services business that serve the biopharma, food, environmental, safety and applied end markets to accelerate scientific outcomes. Since 1937, PerkinElmer has served as a trusted partner in laboratory analysis and management and today complements its service offerings with a broad portfolio of atomic spectroscopy, molecular spectroscopy, and chromatography instruments, consumables, and reagents. With a dedicated team of more than 5,000 team members, the Company serves customers in more than 35 countries. Additional information is available at www.perkinelmer.com

Purpose

PerkinElmer is seeking a Director, Product Management to serve as the full strategic and commercial owner of a product segment within one of its analytical instrument business units. This is a purpose-built strategic leadership role. Reporting to the VP Product Line, the Strategic PM holds end-to-end accountability for the product segment's roadmap, commercial positioning, pricing strategy, and P&L contribution. This role is structurally protected from operational distraction. Day-to-day portfolio execution — quality escalations, SKU management, supply chain issues — is managed by a dedicated Operations PM. This design ensures the Strategic PM can focus entirely on what creates long-term value: the evidence-based product strategy, NPI business cases, and commercial positioning that drive revenue growth and durable competitive differentiation.

Responsibilities

Product Strategy & Roadmap

  • Define and own the 3–5 years product roadmap for the assigned product segment — prioritisation, sequencing, and investment trade-off decisions across instruments, consumables, and software
  • Develop rigorous NPI business cases: market sizing, competitive positioning, financial modelling, and customer value quantification — to a standard that supports VP and CTO gate approval
  • Own gate progression for all NPIs within the segment from concept through commercial launch approval
  • Translate Market Requirements Documents from Strategic Segment Managers into specific product requirements and R&D briefs
  • Drive the long-term technology roadmap in close collaboration with R&D leadership — ensuring the portfolio maintains competitive and technical leadership in priority markets

Voice of Customer & Market Intelligence

  • Build and maintain a structured VOC programme for the product segment — a minimum of 20 in-depth customer conversations per year, focused on requirements validation, competitive intelligence, and pricing research
  • Work in partnership with Strategic Segment Managers to ensure segment-level market requirements are understood and prioritised across the product segment's key end markets
  • Monitor the competitive landscape continuously — new instrument introductions, pricing moves, partnership activity — and translate intelligence into positioning and roadmap responses

Pricing & Financial Performance

  • Own global base pricing strategy for the product segment — setting, communicating, and periodically reviewing instrument and consumable pricing with VP Product Line approval
  • Manage the product segment's P&L contribution in partnership with the VP — tracking revenue, gross margin, and portfolio profitability against AOP targets
  • Support AOP planning with NPI revenue projections, volume forecasts, and portfolio investment requirements

Team Leadership

  • Lead and develop NPI PMs and the Operations PM within the product segment team — setting clear role expectations, performance objectives, and development plans
  • Coach NPI PMs to develop strong business case skills, customer interviewing capability, and commercial programme discipline
  • Build a team culture focused on customer insight, strategic rigour, and commercial accountability
  • Ensure clean handoffs between NPI PM (launch responsibility) and Operations PM (ongoing portfolio execution) — maintaining role clarity and avoiding scope creep

Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Partner with the VP Product Line on portfolio investment prioritisation, AOP planning, and executive gate reviews
  • Work closely with R&D to translate commercial requirements into technically feasible product specifications, maintaining a clear PM/R&D boundary
  • Collaborate with the Sr. Director, Strategic & Commercial Marketing to ensure segment intelligence inputs are incorporated into roadmap and positioning decisions
  • Engage with Regional Product Managers to ensure field market intelligence is incorporated into product and launch planning

Qualifications & Experience

Required

  • 10–15+ years of experience in product management, product strategy, or commercial leadership in analytical instrumentation or scientific equipment
  • Demonstrated experience owning a product roadmap and leading NPI programmes through full commercialisation
  • Direct technical knowledge of the relevant product segment (e.g., atomic spectroscopy, chromatography, materials characterisation) and its key application markets
  • Strong financial acumen — experience managing product line P&L, building NPI business cases, and setting pricing strategy
  • Proven track record of leading and developing small product management teams
  • Ability to travel 25–30% for customer visits, conferences, and internal reviews
  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline

Preferred

  • Advanced degree (MSc, PhD) in a relevant scientific discipline
  • Experience in a structured stage-gate NPI environment
  • Experience working in a matrixed organisation alongside segment marketing, technical, and regional commercial functions
  • Strong executive presence — ability to present product investment decisions clearly to senior leadership and major customers

The annual compensation range for this full-time position is $170,000 to $200,000. The final base pay offered to the successful candidate will be determined by factors including internal equity, work location, as well as individual qualifications, such as job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

title: Engineering Technician 5
description:
About this Job

Engineering Technician 5 (Traffic Engineering Data Collection)

The Louisiana Department of Transportation and Development (DOTD) is seeking a motivated and dependable Engineering Technician 5 to join the Headquarters Traffic Engineering Section in Baton Rouge. This position coordinates advanced traffic data collection activities and reviews traffic engineering studies, plans, and specifications to improve the safety and efficiency of Louisiana’s transportation network. Typical assignments include Complete Streets and Vulnerable Road User (VRU) studies, speed-setting studies, traffic signal design and optimization, and plan reviews.

The ideal candidate is a technically skilled, analytical, and detail-oriented self-starter who can coordinate multiple assignments independently and quickly learn new concepts, technologies, and techniques. Applicants with experience in traffic data collection and analysis, traffic studies, CADD, technical plan review, or applying traffic engineering standards and manuals are encouraged to apply.

Please visit our DOTD Career Center for more information about our agency:

Minimum Qualifications

Possession of a high school diploma or GED plus three years of sub-professional engineering experience; OR

Six months of experience in sub-professional engineering, heavy mobile equipment operation, or mobile equipment maintenance plus three years of sub-professional engineering experience; OR

Eighteen semester hours in one of the following specialized fields: architecture, cartography, construction management, construction technology, drafting, engineering, engineering graphics, engineering technology, industrial technology, landscape architecture, math, or physics.

Job Specification

The official job specifications for this role, as defined by the State Civil Service, can be found here.

Job Duties and Other Information

Job Duties:

  • Coordinates traffic data collection activities with District personnel and other appropriate parties.
  • Leads traffic data collection and analysis activities, including manual peak-hour turning movement counts, 24-hour machine volume counts, speed studies, intersection diagrams, collision diagrams, and other related traffic studies.
  • Compiles, analyzes, and presents traffic data in a usable format and develops recommendations for corrective action.
  • Uses Computer-Aided Design and Drafting (CADD) software to develop traffic control plans, traffic signal inventories, and other traffic-related designs.
  • Reviews traffic engineering studies, plans, and specifications, including speed studies, pedestrian crosswalk studies, traffic signal plans, traffic equipment specifications, and traffic sign plans.
  • Assists with developing scopes for traffic engineering data collection services for Traffic Engineering, Project Management, Planning, Environmental, and other DOTD sections.
  • Communicates and coordinates with consultants, plan development engineers, planners, project managers, District Traffic Operations Engineers, and other stakeholders regarding traffic engineering studies and data collection activities.
  • Assists with developing and updating traffic engineering policies, procedures, standards, and specifications.
  • Attends public meetings and provides technical support to project teams, as needed.
  • Performs other duties as assigned, including emergency or disaster support activities.


Position-Specific Details:

Appointment Type: This position may be filled by probational appointment, promotion, or detail to special duty in accordance with applicable State Civil Service rules.

Compensation: This position receives premium pay of $2.00 per hour for all hours worked.

Additional compensation may be considered for applicants who possess extraordinary job-related qualifications or credentials in accordance with State Civil Service Rule 6.5(g) and DOTD policy. Any additional compensation is subject to approval, verification, and applicable pay limitations.

How To Apply:

No Civil Service test score is required to be considered for this vacancy.

title: Building Inspector (Buildings, Safety Engineering & Environmental Department)
description:
Description

Building Inspector
Buildings Safety Engineering and Environmental Department

The Buildings, Safety, Engineering, and Environmental Department (BSEED) mission is to provide for the safety, health, and welfare of the general public as it pertains to buildings and their environs in an efficient, cost-effective, user-friendly, and professional manner.

BSEED enforces construction, property maintenance, environmental compliance, and zoning codes, which preserve and enhance property values and promote quality of life to make Detroit a preferred place to reside and conduct business.

Under general supervision, inspects new and existing buildings, structures, and signs to ensure compliance with regulatory codes and city ordinances, approved plans, specifications, and accepted standards and methods of work; examines plans for compliance with regulatory codes, laws, and ordinances for the approval of applications for permits.

Examples of Duties

  1. Inspects the use of land and all types and sizes of buildings including residential, commercial, industrial and public buildings, and signs and structures for conformance with the building codes.
  2. Inspects the construction of new buildings, signs and structures with regard to materials, dimensions and work methods used and against approved plans and specifications and codes.
  3. Inspects completed new buildings, signs and structures for conformance to code provisions.
  4. Investigates complaints of unsafe or unlawful conditions of buildings and signs.
  5. Performs routine inspections of existing signs and buildings such as multiple dwellings and places of public assembly to determine whether such buildings and structures conform to applicable codes and ordinances.
  6. Investigates building alterations or repairs to determine whether a building permit is required or has been obtained.
  7. Inspects buildings damaged by fire, estimates the amount of damage and determines whether such buildings may be repaired or should be razed.
  8. Investigates complaints of violations of codes, prepares notices of violation and performs re-inspections of premises or equipment to determine corrections of code violations.
  9. Compiles information and prepares code violation cases for court and appears and testifies regarding code violations in court cases.
  10. Examines plans prior to the issuance of permits to assess conformance with the “state housing law” portion of the building code and zoning ordinance and recommends changes to plans, as required.
  11. Approves applications for permits.
  12. Prepares daily activities reports.

Minimum Qualifications


  • High School Graduation or GED.
  • Four years of recent journey worker-level experience in the construction of buildings and related structures.
Licenses, Certifications, and Other Special Requirements:
  • Employees certified or promoted to this class must acquire and maintain registration as an inspector and plan reviewer with the State of Michigan, as required under the provisions of Public Act #407. Progress toward obtaining certification will be evaluated at the end of the initial six-month probation period with a conditional six-month extension possible, after which, failure to comply will result in termination of employment in this class.
  • Employees in this class will be required to provide and operator a motor vehicle on a reimbursed mileage basis, a valid State of Michigan Operator license is required.

EQUIVALENCY

  • Equivalent combinations of education and experience that provide the required knowledge, skills, and abilities will be evaluated on an individual basis.

Supplemental Information


Evaluation Plan

  • Computerized Exam: 35%
  • Interview: 35%
  • Evaluation of Training, Experience & Personal Qualifications: 30%
  • Total Computerized Exam, Interview and Evaluation T.E.P: 100%
Additional points may be awarded for:
  • Veteran Points: 0 – 15 points
  • Detroit Residency Credit: 15 points


Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
  • Knowledge of materials, operations, construction, and trade practices related to building construction.
  • Knowledge of elementary structural engineering principles governing the construction of buildings.
  • Skill in observation.
  • Skill in reading and interpreting plans and specifications.
  • Skill in communicating effectively, both orally and in writing, with tact and diplomacy.
  • Skill in physical and mechanical dexterity.
  • Ability to display initiative and resourcefulness in performance of duties including handling inspection problems.
  • Ability to detect potential hazards.
  • Ability to climb ladders and enter manholes, narrow openings and crawl spaces and to move along narrow, exposed platforms and beams.
  • Ability to work in high and/or confines spaces.
  • Ability to willfully work in hot, dusty areas.
  • Ability to withstand noxious odors.
  • Ability to interact effectively with the public, peers and other departmental personnel.
  • Ability to willfully acquire additional knowledge and education to remain current in the field.

Candidates considered for placement in this classification may be subject to a Criminal Background Investigation based on the requirements of the position.


DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS:
  • Fieldwork includes exposure to outside elements and seasonal weather conditions and indoor exposure to residential, commercial or industrial property in various conditions and stages of repair or construction.
  • Customer contacts require a neat and clean appearance

title: Program Manager - Quality Excellence
description:
About Us

SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. Powered by two trusted, global brands, Shark and Ninja, the company has a proven track record of bringing disruptive innovation to market and developing one consumer product after another has allowed SharkNinja to enter multiple product categories, driving significant growth and market share gains. Headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts with more than 4,100 associates, the company’s products are sold at key retailers, online and offline, and through distributors around the world.

AI at SharkNinja

At SharkNinja, we’re building an AI-native culture. We’re not waiting for the future; we’re creating it. Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. If you believe the best way to do your job hasn’t been invented yet, you’ll fit right in.

Position Overview:

SharkNinja is building a new Product Excellence Program Management (PEPM) team — three roles, each owning a distinct phase of the product development lifecycle, working together to run one PE operating standard across the full lifecycle from inception to end-of-life.

The vision is simple: four pods, one PE playbook — run faster. Consistent gates, escalation, and star reporting from Inception to EOL. Predicting star ratings before P0. Cutting in-market signal-to-fix to 10 days.

Today, the handoffs across Product Excellence are not seamless enough. Quality insights generated upstream do not always reach the right downstream teams in time. In-market signals do not always make it back into NPD fast enough to influence the next generation. These three roles exist to close that loop — with speed.

The ask for every PEPM is the same: Communicate. Act fast. Ensure the PE point of view is front and center. Each role is embedded at a specific phase of the development cycle, but all three operate as one team — sharing a common operating rhythm, a common PE playbook, and a shared accountability for ensuring nothing falls through the cracks between phases.

All three roles report into VP, Product Excellence and Chief of Staff, and work in close partnership with each other, with the Product Excellence Functional leaders.

Why This Team Exists:

When the team is operating at its best: star prediction is running at every P0, every <4.5★ action is tracked to closure, and every STOP Production, JIRA, and RCCA is resolved inside 30 days.

The PEPM team embodies all pillars of the PE mission:

  1. Voice of the Consumer — ensuring consumer signal drives every program decision, not just the ones that are easy to act on.
  1. 5★ satisfaction — holding the standard at every gate, from the first concept review to the last in-market quality call.
  1. Lower cost of quality — finding and fixing issues early, before the consumer does.
  1. Improved speed of innovation — removing friction between PE insight and engineering action so SharkNinja can move faster without moving blind.

The Three Roles:

  1. Up Front PEPM — Inception to P2:
  1. Connect the future product roadmap to Product Inception (PI), Supply Chain & Retail (SC&R), Continuous Improvement (CI), QA teardowns, and testing — ensuring PE requirements are visible and tracked from the earliest program touchpoint.
  1. Track VEGA Hack completion at P0, ensuring all early-stage quality and consumer experience actions are formally captured and closed.
  1. Own the PE star prediction tracker — managing ACE status across the portfolio and driving actions on any program trending below 4.5 stars before it reaches the P2 gate.
  1. Manage competitive samples and test tracking, ensuring the PE organization has the right reference data to make informed development decisions.
  1. Represent PE in ACE Reviews, ACE End-of-Week responses, and Geo Expansion Exec forums for the Inception-to-P2 phase.
  1. NPD PEPM — P2 to 6 Months in Field:
  1. Be the voice of Product Excellence in weekly Product Reviews — tracking program health, surfacing risks, and ensuring PE requirements stay visible and actioned throughout active development.
  1. Track EB0 and Pre-MP VEGA Hack completion, holding Engineering and Product Development accountable for on-time close-out.
  1. Hold Testing and SC&R accountable to delivery — escalating when milestones slip and ensuring no program reaches launch with unresolved quality or certification gaps.
  1. Act as the central PMO/TPM escalation point for the NPD phase, connecting Risk Assessments to Boston and London teams and ensuring cross-functional visibility of program health.
  1. Represent PE in Product NPD Reviews, In-Person Reviews, and Weekly Category L1 Roundtables.
  1. In-Market PEPM — 6 Months in Field to End-of-Life:
  1. Flag in-market star dips in real time — with active focus on any SKU below 4.0 stars and proactive awareness of anything below 4.5 stars. A star dip is not a report; it is a trigger for action.
  1. Own STOP Production tracking and communications, ensuring the right stakeholders are informed and corrective actions are moving at pace.
  1. Track JIRA closures and Root Cause & Corrective Action (RCCA) completion to systemic resolution — with a target of all STOP/JIRA/RCCA closed inside 30 days.
  1. Represent PE in Weekly PE Category Reviews (rotating category) and Geo Expansion Exec forums.

Who We Are Looking For:

We are hiring three people into this team, and the right candidates share a common profile but bring specific depth in their phase of the development cycle.

  • Required (all three roles):

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
description:
About the Role

This is a Senior Machine Learning Engineer role embedded within a growing AI and Data Science team at a healthcare-focused data and analytics company. You'll take end-to-end ownership of enterprise-scale ML solutions — from raw data through to production — playing a critical part in delivering compliant, high-impact AI capabilities in a regulated healthcare environment.

What You'll Do

  • Design, develop, deploy, and maintain enterprise-scale machine learning solutions from the ground up.

  • Build end-to-end ML pipelines covering data ingestion, feature engineering, model training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and retraining.

  • Develop and maintain MLOps pipelines including CI/CD, model registry, feature stores, automated deployment, and rollback strategies.

  • Monitor production models for drift, accuracy degradation, and overall system health.

  • Develop REST APIs and integrate ML services into enterprise cloud applications.

  • Optimize models for latency, scalability, reliability, and cost.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Data Engineers, Software Engineers, Product Managers, and Clinical teams.

  • Provide technical leadership on AI/ML initiatives and ensure compliance with HIPAA, PHI, and PII standards.

What We're Looking For

  • 8+ years of professional software engineering and machine learning experience.

  • Strong healthcare industry background — this is a firm requirement.

  • Deep expertise across the full ML lifecycle: preprocessing, feature engineering, model development, calibration, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance.

  • Hands-on MLOps experience with strong Python and SQL skills.

  • Proficiency with distributed computing (Apache Spark) and Databricks in production environments.

  • Experience with at least one major cloud platform (Azure, AWS, or GCP).

  • Familiarity with MLflow, Feature Stores, Model Registries, Docker, and Git.

  • Experience building and integrating REST APIs; strong debugging and performance-tuning skills.

  • Working knowledge of HIPAA compliance requirements when handling sensitive healthcare data.

  • Nice to have: LLMs in production, RAG/prompt engineering, GenAI, Kubernetes, Scala, or managed ML platforms (Azure ML, SageMaker, Vertex AI).

  • US work authorization required; visa sponsorship is not available.

Compensation & Benefits

Hourly contract rate of $70–$75/hr on W2, equivalent to approximately $145,600–$156,000 annually. This is a contract (W2) engagement. Visa sponsorship is not available.

Location

Based in Palo Alto, CA. Work arrangement details to be confirmed with the hiring team.

title: Program Specialist
description:
Department Information


Residency Requirement

This position is open to current Colorado residents only.

Please note: This recruitment may be used to fill multiple vacancies.


Division of Child Support Services

The Division of Child Support Services (DCSS) exists to ensure that all children receive financial and medical support from each parent through the location of each parent, the establishment of paternity and support obligations, and the enforcement of those obligations and connection to resources to assist parents in overcoming any barriers that are impeding their ability to pay child support.


The Systems and Operations Section encompasses three major areas: Automated Child Support Enforcement System (ACSES) development and support; the Family Support Registry (FSR), Colorado’s mandated State Disbursement Unit (SDU)The FSR was created and provides services per Colorado Revised Statutes 26-13-114. FSR services are for all families with a support order.


The FSR is split into two sections. FSR Financial Services (FFS) is responsible for the operation of the State Disbursement Unit (SDU). FSR Support Services (FSS) provides services to employers, families, county Child Support Services (CSS) offices, and the court.


The State Disbursement Unit, which executes the Division’s annual responsibilities to receive and deliver payments totaling over $520 million annually to families. In addition, FFS staff provide financial services to families and county CSS offices. The FSR Financial Services Unit includes six State FTE and vendor services, and the Unit is responsible for the procurement and ongoing administration of associated contractual services that total over $2 million annually. This position works in the FSR Financial Services Unit.


The FSR’s Financial Services Unit is responsible for using established guidelines and procedures to perform State financial reconciliations between the contract vendor, the FSR Bank, the ACSES, Colorado Department of Human Services (CDHS), and the sixty-four (64) county CSS programs.


Description of Job

Weekly Hybrid Working Arrangements

Minimum 2 days In Office and Maximum 3 days Remote Work

Please note: Work arrangements are subject to change at any time.

This position is responsible for monitoring and ensuring the quality assurance of FSR operations and activities with respective stakeholders; serves as a liaison between CDHS-CSS, FSR contractors, and county CSS units on issues/activities performed by the FSR; assists with developing procedures and rules to ensure compliance with the terms of the FSR contract(s) and any associated amendment(s) related to payment processing, customer service, and electronic payment card.


This position collaborates with the FSR contractor(s), county CSS units, and Colorado Department of Human Services (CDHS) staff to enhance and improve FSR service delivery to FSR stakeholders; takes action to rectify deficiencies and problems within various areas of FSR operations; identifies and reports exceptions and conditions requiring resolution to the FSR contractor(s); tracks these exceptions and ensures their resolution; and produces various reports to document, verify, and provide archival reference to substantiate all related activities.


This position provides oversight, monitoring, review, and analysis of the FSR operations on an ongoing basis to ensure contract compliance by all FSR contract vendors; identifies and reports exceptions and conditions that require contractor resolution; follows up on contractor resolutions and implements procedures to improve processes; monitors performance using statistics obtained through the State system and information reported by the contractors; performs on-site visits at the FSR facility(s) to review and monitor operations, practices, and compliance with contract requirements; samples work production to ensure compliance is at acceptable error rates for payment processing, customer service, and electronic payment card services; performs contract audits and reviews the annual self-audit reports prepared by each contractor; ensures the contractors are in compliance; provides support, training, and guidance to contractors on how to handle difficult or unusual situations as needed; assists the Supervisor with the contract procurement process; requires training in CDHS contract management and is a member of the CDHS Contract User’s Group; and ensures that CDHS and FSR contractors’ operational and procedural manuals are accurate, complete, up-to-date, and supported by respective technical and/or system requirements.

This position may assume the lead on projects related to their subject matter expertise. This includes documenting the purpose of the project; identifying the scope of the project; researching the law, and CSS policies and procedures; creating/implementing test plans; drafting business rules and procedures; providing project status updates; keeping the project on task; and providing training as needed.


This position identifies areas in the ACSES where improvement can be made. This includes assisting with identifying system changes required to support such improvements; ensuring Program procedures, policies, methods, and internal controls necessary to operate the FSR on a daily basis are followed; ensuring procedures, policies, methods and internal controls that effectively account for and manage the FSR activities are followed in accordance with the contractual agreement; and establishing methods and procedures not only to outline issues but also to facilitate and expedite their resolution.


This position ensures that FSR and/or FSR contractor(s) operational and procedural manuals are accurate, complete, up to date, and supported by respective technical and/or system requirements.


This position develops and provides training, reference materials, and guidance to maximize the functionality of the FSR operations, CDHS-CSS Program business, and supported automated systems. Systems include but are not limited to: ACSES, eCSE. Training is provided on an as-needed basis to respective stakeholders to ensure that all services are delivered in accordance with the terms and conditions of the contract and legislative Program requirements. This also includes ensuring appropriate CDHS or Fiscal Agent manual(s), instructions, and procedures and processes are identified, updated, and referenced to support the training.


This position develops and establishes procedures and processes to troubleshoot, answer, resolve, and investigate system and programmatic exceptions, complaints, and inquiries. This includes researching and documenting problems, determining the course of action to expedite resolution, and recommending action plans to close issues. Where inquiries result in system use and/or policy changes, this position provides information, training, and guidance to related entities or users; and updates appropriate manuals, instructions, procedures and processes to reflect the changes. This position also assists the Unit Supervisor with developing and delivering training curriculum related to the position responsibilities to cross-train other members of the Unit.


This position provides customer service and technical assistance to county CSS units and FSR staff related to system and program reviews, corrective action plans and options, and FSR and CSS functions; makes recommendations to counties and FSR contractors’ managers regarding Program direction and requirements; and serves as a liaison between CDHS-CSS, FSR contractors, and county CSS units.

This position is part of the team of individuals that address customer complaints pertaining to the FSR. Complaints received through the front desk, supervisor assignment, or contractor’s request for assistance. This position is responsible for documenting the issue, researching the events that led to the complaint, and working with the customer to find a win-win resolution.


Other duties as assigned that are reasonably within the scope of the position classification, including coverage of staff absences; completion of special projects, completion of the grant or temporary assignments; representation of the Unit, Division, or Department on task forces or committees; and completion of other supervisory designated tasks.

Job Duties:

  • Non-IV-D Case Management
  • Contract Management
  • Program Support/Training
  • Customer Service
  • Other Duties as Assigned

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions of Employment & Appeal Rights


Minimum Qualifications:

Six (6) years of relevant experience in an occupation related to the work assigned to this position with a minimum of the following:

  • Demonstrated two (2) years of experience in writing procedures

  • Demonstrated three (3) years of experience in Child Support Services

  • Demonstrated experience in being a liaison between several departments

- OR -

Education:

A combination of related education in Accounting, Business, Human Services, Finance, or a closely related field and relevant experience in an occupation related to the work assigned equal to six (6) years with a minimum of the following:

  • Demonstrated two (2) years of experience in writing procedures

  • Demonstrated three (3) years of child support services

  • Demonstrated experience in being a liaison between several departments



Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience writing business rules

  • Experience delivering training

  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy

  • Proficient in Microsoft Suite/Google Suite

  • Experience using ACSES (Automated Child Support Enforcement System)

  • COWINS Partnership Agreement: Relevant years of State service should be considered as a preferred qualification and given weight under the process. Part-time relevant years of State service will be prorated.

  • TRANSFERS ONLY: Relevant years of State service will be considered as a preferred qualification and given the weight of at least 15% of the overall score under the process.

  • Relevant years of State service contribute to a candidate's position-related knowledge, skill, ability, behavior, or other posted competency


Conditions of Employment:

  • 1075 background check (access to Federal Tax information) and reference check required.

  • This position requires State of Colorado residency at the time of application (unless otherwise identified in the posting), and residency within the state throughout the duration of employment in this position.

  • Travel - Position may be required to travel throughout the State on a frequent basis to meet with and provide training to county partners or to travel out of state to annual conferences

  • Former State employees who were disciplinarily terminated or resigned in lieu of termination must:

    • Disclose that information on the application.

    • Explain why the prior termination or resignation should not disqualify you from the current position.

    • Provide your employee number from your prior State employment. Absent extraordinary circumstances, prior disciplinary termination or resignation in lieu

    • of termination and failure to provide this information will disqualify the applicant from future State employment with CDHS.

CDHS Selection Process Explanation:

Employment history is calculated on a full-time basis (40/hours per week). Part-time employment is calculated on a prorated basis to determine qualifications. Be sure your application specifically addresses your qualifications, experience, work products, and accomplishments as they relate to the position and minimum requirements.

  • Preferred Qualifications & Competencies:

    • Relevant years of state service experience.


Minimum Qualification Screening Process:

A Human Resources Analyst will review the work experience/job duties sections of the online job application to determine whether your experience meets the minimum qualifications for the position. You must complete the official State of Colorado online application. Cover letters and resumes WILL NOT be reviewed during the minimum qualifications screening process. You must specifically document your work experience and qualifications in the application form. Do not use "see resume" or "see attached."

You must meet the minimum qualifications to continue in the selection process. Part-time work experience will be prorated.

Comparative Analysis Process – Structured Application Review:

After minimum qualification screening, the comparative analysis process will involve reviewing and rating of all the information you submit. The comparative analysis step may also include your results from standardized testing.

Your Work Experience/Job Duties:

Document your work experience/job duties to the extent to which you possess the skills, education, experience, minimum qualifications, and preferred qualifications. Ensure this information is documented in the Work Experience section of the application.

If listed, answer all supplemental questions as your answers to these questions will be evaluated during this phase. Provide at least 4-8 sentences for each supplemental question.

Supplemental Questions:

Answer the supplemental questions completely and thoughtfully. We will rate your answers based on the content of your response and your writing skills (spelling, grammar, and clarity of your writing).

Appeal Rights:

You may file an appeal with the State Personnel Board or request a review by the State Personnel Director if your application is eliminated. You will find the appeals process, the official appeal form, and how to deliver it on the State Personnel Board website.


  • You or your representative must sign and submit the official appeal form for review.

  • You can find the official appeal form here.

  • You must be deliver the official appeal form to the State Personnel Board:

    • By email (dpa_state.personnelboard@state.co.us), or

    • Postmarked in US Mail to(1525 Sherman Street, 4th Floor, Denver CO 80203, or

    • Hand delivered (1525 Sherman Street, 4th Floor, Denver CO 80203), or

    • Faxed (303.866.5038) within ten (10) calendar days from your receipt of notice or acknowledgement of the department’s action.


Contact the State Personnel Board for assistance:

title: Regional Product Manager Atomic Spectroscopy (REMOTE East Coast)
description:
The Company

PerkinElmer is a global analytical services and solutions provider with offerings including the leading OneSource Field and Laboratory services business that serve the biopharma, food, environmental, safety and applied end markets to accelerate scientific outcomes. Since 1937, PerkinElmer has served as a trusted partner in laboratory analysis and management and today complements its service offerings with a broad portfolio of atomic spectroscopy, molecular spectroscopy, and chromatography instruments, consumables, and reagents. With a dedicated team of more than 5,000 team members, the Company serves customers in more than 35 countries. Additional information is available at www.perkinelmer.com

Purpose

PerkinElmer is seeking a Regional Product Manager to support the commercial organization in the NAM Region and help implement the regional Inorganics strategy. This role coordinates between central product management and the regional sales and marketing teams — providing the product expertise, competitive response capability, and local market intelligence that the field organisation needs to win in customer-facing situations.

The Regional PM is the product line's voice in the field. They are the person a regional sales manager calls when a deal requires deep product knowledge, when a competitor launches a new instrument, or when a key customer wants to understand how the product line meets their specific application needs. They bring the centre's strategic thinking to the region, and the region's market reality back to central product management.

This role will analyze win/loss data, capture critical regional VOC input, facilitate demand creation activities in the region, track regional KPI’s and drive financial performance and actions needed to achieve.

Responsibilities:

Field Commercial Support

  • Provide real-time product expertise to the regional sales team — answering technical and commercial questions, supporting customer demonstrations, and participating in key account meetings where product management presence creates commercial advantage
  • Lead regional competitive response: providing timely, accurate, and commercially useful guidance to the sales team when a competitor launches a new instrument, adjusts pricing, or makes a specific claim in a customer situation
  • Support regional sales management with product mix analysis, product line forecasting inputs, and portfolio utilisation data that helps the region prioritise selling effort
  • Participate in distributor management where the product line is sold through channel partners — providing product training, commercial support, and competitive tools

Launch Localisation & Execution

  • Lead the regional execution of global product launches — adapting central launch plans to regional market conditions, regulatory requirements, and commercial priorities
  • Coordinate with Regional Marketing Managers to ensure launch campaigns, customer events, and demand generation activities reflect the product line's commercial priorities in the region
  • Manage regional beta programmes in partnership with the NPI PM — identifying and engaging appropriate regional beta sites, managing relationships, and ensuring feedback is captured and reported to the central programme team
  • Deliver regional sales training on new product launches — ensuring field commercial teams can demonstrate, position, and close against competitive alternatives from day one of launch

Market Intelligence & Feedback

  • Serve as the regional intelligence feed to central product management — systematically reporting competitive activity, customer feedback, application trends, and market developments that are visible in the field but not from the centre
  • Conduct customer conversations specifically focused on market intelligence: competitive usage patterns, unmet application needs, pricing sensitivity, and regional regulatory trends
  • Attend and represent PerkinElmer at regional scientific conferences, trade shows, and customer events — gathering competitive intelligence and building relationships with key opinion leaders in the region
  • Provide the Strategic PM with documented regional input on product requirements, pricing feedback, and application priorities as part of the Customer Outcome Document and roadmap process

Customer & Stakeholder Relationships

  • Build and maintain relationships with key regional customers — particularly those who are opinion leaders, early adopters, or large-volume buyers whose satisfaction is strategically important to the product line's regional performance
  • Support key account teams with product-specific technical and commercial input for major tenders, framework agreements, and long-cycle strategic accounts
  • Partner with the Applications Scientist to support customer demonstrations, method development assistance, and application-specific support for key regional opportunities

Qualifications & Experience

Required

  • 5–10 years of experience in product management, technical sales, applications science, or commercial marketing within analytical instrumentation or scientific equipment
  • Broad working knowledge of at least one product line technology (atomic spectroscopy, chromatography, materials characterisation) and its key regional application markets
  • Demonstrated ability to operate effectively as a field-based specialist — managing multiple concurrent customer and commercial priorities, often with limited day-to-day management oversight
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills — able to engage credibly with regional sales teams, distributors, and customers across varying technical and commercial contexts
  • Willingness and ability to travel extensively within the assigned region (40–50%)
  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, Physics, or a related scientific discipline

Preferred

  • Advanced degree (MSc, PhD) in a relevant analytical or materials science discipline
  • Direct hands-on laboratory experience with analytical instrumentation in a research, QC, or applications environment — giving the Regional PM genuine field credibility with scientifically trained customers
  • Prior experience in a field-based role (applications scientist, field sales specialist, or field marketing) that required operating across multiple customer sites and managing competing priorities without close supervision
  • Native or near-native fluency in the primary commercial language of the assigned region (where English is not the dominant commercial language)

The annual compensation range for this full-time position is $120,000 to $155,000. The final base pay offered to the successful candidate will be determined by factors including internal equity, work location, as well as individual qualifications, such as job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

description:
Description

Who we are. We protect lives. The Georgia Department of Public Health is the lead agency entrusted by the people of Georgia to proudly protect lives and promote healthy lifestyles in diverse communities statewide. We are committed to preventing disease, injury, and disability; promoting health and well-being; and preparing the State of Georgia for responding to disasters.

What we offer. As a member of the Georgia Department of Public Health team, you will join a passionate group of individuals who are dedicated to making an impact. No matter your role, you will individually contribute to protecting the lives of all Georgians while receiving a wide range of benefits, so you can:

  • Make a Professional Impact – Build your career where it matters and protect lives in the community where you live, work, and play
  • Enjoy Workplace Flexibility – Experience flexibility in how you work so you can be your best self for you and Georgia Residents
  • Work with a Dynamic and Diverse Team– Collaborative and inclusive way of working where employees share ideas and leverage collective strengths
  • Achieve Career Longevity – Countless opportunities for continuous learning/development that support a long-term career
  • Take Part in a Hands-on Working Culture – Unique culture of active engagement and problem-solving, no matter your role
  • Feel Pride in Where you Work – Be part of making an impact in public health alongside dedicated people just like you

As a Health & Safety Inspector within the Columbus Health Department at the Georgia Department of Public Health, you will join a dedicated group of public health professionals that help support the overall mission and vision of protecting lives of Georgian residents in a variety of ways.

Job Responsibilities

This position will be based in Columbus, GA and will perform a variety of duties in support of the vector control team. You will support the Department by utilizing your expertise to fulfill the following responsibilities:

  • Inspect breeding areas and apply insecticides/rodenticides to infected areas
  • Measure, mix, and store insecticides and rodenticides properly
  • safely operate government vehicles and pest control equipment.
  • Assist in emergency preparedness including pandemic efforts and response.

* Work hours for this position will be 5:30AM - 2:00PM, Monday - Friday

* Must be approved by West Central Health District’s vehicle insurance carrier prior to hire.

Minimum Qualifications

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: HS Diploma or GED. Must have a valid driver’s license, clean MVR and be insurance eligible.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: Moderate to heavy physical activity and consistent exposure to working conditions that may interact with an employee’s medical or fitness condition. May involve heavy lifting (above 45 lbs.), pushing, pulling, extended climbing, crawling, bending, and/or operation of potentially dangerous equipment including motor vehicles.

Additional Information

All West Central Health District 7 employees are deemed essential workers in the event of an emergency. As such, you may be called on to participate in an event including but not limited to: staffing a shelter, working at a Specimen Point of Collection Site (SPOC) and/or working at a Point of Dispensing site (POD). If you are called on to participate, you are required to report to the designated site as a condition of employment, whether the emergency occurs during or outside regular work hours.

Georgia Department of Public Health Commissioner and leaders encourages all employees to engage in regular physical activities and to make lifestyle choices that promote health and well-being. The use of physical breaks during the workday is authorized to support this philosophy and assist employees in meeting their physical goals. A maximum of 30 minutes in a given workday may be used to engage in physical activities, generally in the form of two 15-minute breaks or one 30-minute break.

Employment Information

Current State employees are subject to State Personnel Board rules regarding salary.

DPH accepts educational credential recognized by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) and/or the US Department of Education (DOE) will be considered. DPH will contact educational institutions to verify degree, diploma, licensure, etc.

The candidate selected for this position may be subject to pre-employment drug screening and a criminal background check.

As an employee of DPH, in the event of an identified emergency you may be required, as a term and condition of employment, to assist in meeting the emergency responsibilities of the department.

If you require accommodations under the American Disability Act (ADA), email request by the closing date of this announcement to: DPH-HR@dph.ga.gov.

DPH is an Equal Opportunity Employer

Due to the volume of applications received, we are unable to provide information on application status by phone or e-mail. All qualified applicants will be considered, but may not necessarily receive an interview. Selected applicants will be contacted by the hiring agency for next steps in the selection process. Applicants who are not selected will not receive notification.

This position is subject to close at any time once a satisfactory applicant pool has been identified.

title: Partner Analyst
description:
Trives du med at bygge stærke relationer, omsætte data til handling og drive forbedringer? Så skal du måske være det bindeled, der styrker samarbejdet mellem Verisure og vores servicepartnere.

Hos Verisure søger vi lige nu en struktureret og proaktiv Partner Analyst, der vil spille en yderst vigtig rolle i samarbejdet med vores eksterne servicepartnere og være med til at sikre fremdrift i vores daglige drift og leverancer.

Om rollen

Som Partner Analyst bliver du en nøglespiller i samarbejdet med vores seks eksterne servicepartnere og deres montører. Du får en central rolle i at styrke relationerne gennem tæt dialog, løbende sparring og opfølgning på resultater. Samtidig sikrer du koordinering mellem forskellige interne og eksterne interessenter, så samarbejdet fungerer optimalt.

Rollen kombinerer struktur, stakeholder management og analytisk tænkning. Du bliver den naturlige sparringspartner for vores servicepartnere og får et indgående kendskab til deres leverancer og udviklingsmuligheder. Med afsæt i virksomhedens strategi omsætter du ambitioner til konkrete initiativer, sikrer implementering og følger op på, at vi skaber de ønskede resultater.

Derudover får du mulighed for at præge og videreudvikle arbejdsgange, så de understøtter både effektiv drift og høj kvalitet. Hverdagen er dynamisk og præget af mange interessenter, så vi forventer, at du tager initiativ, tænker løsningsorienteret og trives med at navigere i komplekse problemstillinger, hvor der ikke altid findes en fastlagt vej frem.

Dine opgaver

  • Skabe og styrke relationerne til vores eksterne servicepartnere gennem tæt dialog og løbende sparring.
  • Analysere data, nøgletal og performance på daglig basis for at identificere trends, indsatsområder og muligheder for forbedring.
  • Være bindeled mellem partnere og interne interessenter ved at koordinere forespørgsler, følge op på udfordringer og sikre fremdrift.
  • Formidle nye initiativer, arbejdsgange og forventninger på en klar og engagerende måde.
  • Bidrage til projekter og udviklingsaktiviteter, der understøtter optimering af processer og samarbejdsformer.
  • Sikre, at aftaler, indsatser og opfølgninger bliver omsat til konkrete resultater.
  • Stillingen indebærer fra tid til anden rejser til vores servicepartnere rundt omkring i Danmark.

Din profil

  • Du er nyuddannet eller i starten af din karriere med en relevant videregående uddannelse.
  • Du har erfaring med dataanalyse, Excel og PowerBI.
  • Du behersker engelsk i både tale og skrift.
  • Du har stærke samarbejds- og kommunikationsevner og trives i en udadvendt rolle.
  • Du arbejder struktureret og trives med at finde løsninger i en kompleks og omskiftelig hverdag.
  • Du er proaktiv og motiveres af ansvar og muligheden for at løbe selvstændigt med opgaver.

Vil du være en del af Verisure og være med til at gøre en forskel?

Har du spørgsmål til stillingen, kan du kontakte HR Business Partner & Operations Manager Emilie Boysen på emilie.m.aakerwall@verisure.com.

Vi vil løbende gennemgå ansøgninger og afholde interviews, så vi opfordrer dig til at søge stillingen hurtigst muligt.

Hos Verisure arbejder vi for at fremme en mangfoldig og inkluderende arbejdsplads. Vi tror på, at diversitet i tanker og baggrund kun gør vores teams stærkere og mere innovative. Vi forpligter os derfor til en kultur præget af diversitet og inklusion med lige muligheder for alle, og opfordrer alle uanset baggrund, kultur, køn, alder og erfaring, til at ansøge om at blive en del af vores team. Vi er mennesker, som beskytter mennesker, og sammen står vi endnu stærkere i vores mission om at skabe tryghed for vores kunder.

Om Verisure

Hos Verisure udfører vores medarbejdere noget fantastisk hver eneste dag. Ved at beskytte det, der betyder mest, ændrer vi livet til det bedre for vores kunder. Vi er den førende europæiske udbyder af professionelt overvågede sikkerhedsløsninger med 24/7 respons og service, og vi er til stede i 18 lande i Europa og Latinamerika. Vi integrerer produktudvikling, design, salg, installation og en 24/7 professionel overvågningsløsning. Vores succes afhænger af vores medarbejdere, og vi investerer i dem hver eneste dag. Hos Verisure bliver du en del af en førende virksomhed inden for branchen.

Vi er Great Place to Work certificeret

Undersøgelsen viser, at vi i Verisure har en åben og inkluderende arbejdsplads, hvor der er plads til at være sig selv, og hvor sammenhold og følelsen af at gøre en forskel bliver anerkendt af vores medarbejdere.

title: Product Manager - AI Neobank App
description:
About KIRA

Our mission is to make money smart, reliable and within reach for everyone.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in Asia and it includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and at ease and self reliance, become an expert. We believe AI will help us achieve this in our generation.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

We are looking for product managers to own product areas within KIRA's AI Neobank App.

This role is for builders who can understand users, define product direction, work with engineering and design, launch fast and keep improving after release.

What You'll Own

  • Own product areas across insurance, payments, savings, investing, travel or other financial services.

  • Define user problems, product scope, success metrics, roadmap and launch plans.

  • Work with engineering, design, data, operations, compliance and business teams.

  • Turn complex financial products into simple, usable customer journeys.

  • Use data, feedback, research and production issues to improve product decisions.

  • Launch features, monitor performance and drive iterations.

  • Make trade-offs between speed, user experience, business impact, compliance and operational complexity.

What We're Looking For

  • Experience as Product Manager, Product Owner, founder, growth/product operator or similar role.

  • Strong product sense and ability to simplify complex workflows.

  • Able to work with engineers and designers to ship real products.

  • Comfortable with metrics, user feedback, experiments and post-launch learning.

  • Strong writing, prioritization and stakeholder management.

  • High ownership and ability to drive work with limited guidance.

  • Experience in fintech, insurance, payments, consumer apps or high-growth products is a strong advantage.

The Kind of Builder We Want

  • Starts from user problems, not feature lists.

  • Can make decisions with incomplete information.

  • Knows how to ship quickly and learn after launch.

  • Works well with engineering without hiding behind process.

  • Honest about what changed because of their work versus wider team effort.

This Role Is Not For

  • People who only write decks and do not drive execution.

  • PMs who cannot work deeply with engineering.

  • Candidates who need perfect data before making decisions.

  • People who launch features and then stop caring.

  • PMs who exaggerate business impact without understanding attribution.

Location

This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Portugal. We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Portugal.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

1. Online assessment or practical task

2. Role-specific interview

3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.
